items.title: [Bug]: API server platform ignores fallback_providers config
items.body:
### Bug Description

The API server platform (`gateway/platforms/api_server.py`) never passes `fallback_model` to `AIAgent()`, so the fallback chain is always empty when requests come through the OpenAI-compatible API endpoint. Fallback works correctly on all other platforms (Telegram, Discord, Slack, etc.).

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure `fallback_providers` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`
2. Connect Open WebUI (or any OpenAI-compatible client) to the API server at `localhost:8642/v1`
3. Send a message while the primary provider is rate-limited
4. Observe: retries exhaust, fallback attempt silently does nothing, request fails

### Expected Behavior

API server should fall back to the configured `fallback_providers` chain, same as Telegram/Discord/Slack.

### Actual Behavior

`_try_activate_fallback()` returns `False` immediately because `_fallback_chain` is empty — `fallback_model` was never passed to the `AIAgent` constructor.

### Affected Component

API server platform (`gateway/platforms/api_server.py`)

### Hermes Version

v0.7.0 (2026.4.3)

### Root Cause Analysis

In `api_server.py`, `_create_agent()` constructs AIAgent without `fallback_model`:

```python
# api_server.py ~line 432
agent = AIAgent(
    model=model,
    **runtime_kwargs,
    ...
    session_db=self._ensure_session_db(),
    # fallback_model is missing here
)
```

Compare with `gateway/run.py` which correctly passes `fallback_model=self._fallback_model` at lines 4005, 4179, and 5816.

### Proposed Fix

Load the fallback config in `_create_agent()` and pass it through. Either import `GatewayApp._load_fallback_model()` or replicate the simple yaml load inline.

items.title: [Bug]: Memory provider tools fail in sequential tool dispatch path
items.body:
### Bug Description

When a memory provider plugin (e.g. Honcho) registers tools via `get_tool_schemas()`, those tools work correctly in the **concurrent** execution path (`_invoke_tool`) which checks `self._memory_manager.has_tool()`. However, the **sequential** execution path (`_execute_tool_calls_sequential`) has no equivalent check — it dispatches `todo`, `session_search`, `memory`, `clarify`, `delegate_task`, then falls through directly to `handle_function_call()` →`registry.dispatch()`, which returns `"Unknown tool"` for any memory provider tool.

  This affects all memory provider plugins that expose tools (Honcho, RetainDB, etc.).

### Steps to Reproduce

  1. Configure a memory provider that exposes tools (e.g. `memory.provider: honcho`)
  2. Have the model call a memory provider tool (e.g. `honcho_profile`) in a batch where `_should_parallelize_tool_batch()` returns `False` —
  this happens whenever any tool in the batch is not in `_PARALLEL_SAFE_TOOLS`
  3. The tool returns `{"error": "Unknown tool: honcho_profile"}`

  Cron jobs are the most common trigger since `quiet_mode=True` hits the fallthrough path, and memory provider tools aren't in `_PARALLEL_SAFE_TOOLS`.

### Expected Behavior

Memory provider tools should be dispatched via `self._memory_manager.handle_tool_call()` regardless of whether the sequential or concurrent path is used.


### Actual Behavior

 The model calls `honcho_profile`, `honcho_context`, and `session_search` in a single batch. Since `honcho_profile` and `honcho_context` are
  not in `_PARALLEL_SAFE_TOOLS`, `_should_parallelize_tool_batch()` returns `False` and all three tools are routed through
  `_execute_tool_calls_sequential`.

  `session_search` succeeds (it has a dedicated elif branch), but the two Honcho tools fall through to `handle_function_call()` →
  `registry.dispatch()` which doesn't know about them:

  ```json
  {"error": "Unknown tool: honcho_profile"}
  {"error": "Unknown tool: honcho_context"}

  The model retries both tools individually — same result each time. After exhausting retries, the model gives up on gathering context and
  hallucinates a response based on the (unrelated) session_search results from a previous cron job's summary, producing a factually incorrect
  message to the end user.

  The tools are correctly registered in valid_tool_names and self.tools (confirmed via the system prompt which shows "Honcho Memory: Active
  (hybrid mode)"), and the memory manager's has_tool() returns True for both — the dispatch just never reaches it in the sequential path.
  ```

### Affected Component

Tools (terminal, file ops, web, code execution, etc.)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Operating System

Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS

### Python Version

Python 3.12.3

### Hermes Version

v0.6.0

### Relevant Logs / Traceback

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

_No response_

### Proposed Fix (optional)

 Two changes in `run_agent.py`:

  **1. Add memory\_manager dispatch to `_execute_tool_calls_sequential`**, between the `delegate_task` elif and the `quiet_mode` fallthrough:

  ```python
  elif self._memory_manager and self._memory_manager.has_tool(function_name):
      function_result = self._memory_manager.handle_tool_call(function_name, function_args)
      tool_duration = time.time() - tool_start_time

  2. Add memory provider tool names to _PARALLEL_SAFE_TOOLS (or better: have the set dynamically include tools from registered memory
  providers, since they are read-only or idempotent by design).

items.title: feat: memory provider discovery should scan user-installed plugins
items.body:
## Problem

The memory provider discovery system (`plugins/memory/__init__.py`) only scans the bundled `plugins/memory/` directory inside the hermes-agent source tree. Memory provider plugins installed via `hermes plugins install` (which clones to `~/.hermes/plugins/`) are invisible to `hermes memory setup` and `hermes memory status`.

This means user-installed memory providers require a manual symlink:

```bash
ln -s ~/.hermes/plugins/<provider_name> \
      ~/.hermes/hermes-agent/plugins/memory/<provider_name>
```

This is not discoverable and breaks on `hermes update` (which can reset the source tree).

## Proposed fix

`discover_memory_providers()` and `load_memory_provider()` in `plugins/memory/__init__.py` should also scan `$HERMES_HOME/plugins/` for directories containing `__init__.py` that implement `MemoryProvider`. Bundled plugins should take precedence when both locations provide the same name.

Similarly, `_install_dependencies()` in `hermes_cli/memory_setup.py` should search both locations when resolving `plugin.yaml` for pip dependency lists.

## Context

This came up while integrating the [Observational Memory](https://github.com/intertwine/hermes-observational-memory) provider as a standalone plugin. The bundled version in #4787 works fine, but the standalone install path requires the workaround above.

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Description

The WhatsApp platform adapter (`gateway/platforms/whatsapp.py`) does not override `send_voice()` from the base class. The base class fallback sends the audio file path as plain text (e.g. `🔊 Audio: /path/to/file.ogg`) instead of delivering it as a native voice message.

All other media methods (`send_image`, `send_image_file`, `send_video`, `send_document`) are properly overridden and call `_send_media_to_bridge()`, but `send_voice` was missed.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use TTS (e.g. Edge provider) to generate a voice reply on WhatsApp
2. The user receives a text message with the file path instead of a playable voice note

## Expected Behavior

Voice messages should be delivered as native WhatsApp audio/voice notes, same as other platforms (Telegram works correctly).

## Fix

Add the following override to `WhatsAppAdapter` in `gateway/platforms/whatsapp.py`:

```python
async def send_voice(
    self,
    chat_id: str,
    audio_path: str,
    caption: Optional[str] = None,
    reply_to: Optional[str] = None,
    **kwargs,
) -> SendResult:
    """Send an audio file as a native WhatsApp voice message via bridge."""
    return await self._send_media_to_bridge(chat_id, audio_path, "audio", caption)
```

This is a 3-line fix. Similar to #4339 (Matrix missing voice support).

items.title: [Feature]: Native Google GenAI Provider for Gemini Models
items.body:
### Problem or Use Case

Currently, users wanting to run Gemini models (like gemini-3.1-pro-preview) natively must either use a middleman service or attempt to use Google's OpenAI-compatible endpoint. However, routing through the OpenAI compatibility layer often causes fragile tool calling, dropped streaming tokens, or agent crashes. This happens because of schema translation mismatches between Hermes's strict OpenAI-style loops and Google's actual backend expectations. The use case is to allow developers to drop in a GOOGLE_API_KEY and run Gemini 3.1 Pro natively with 100% stable multi-turn tool calling, uninterrupted streaming, and full context support without relying on fragile wrappers.

### Proposed Solution

Implement a native provider: "google" class in Hermes Agent that communicates directly via the Google GenAI API, bypassing the OpenAI translation layer entirely.
Key technical requirements include:
• Native Schema Translation: Programmatically map Hermes's standard JSON schema for tools into Google's specific FunctionDeclaration format, and correctly intercept functionCall payloads to return them cleanly to the sandbox as functionResponse arrays.
• Message Normalization: Google's API enforces strict role alternation (user, model) in the contents array. The new provider must include a normalizer to merge adjacent messages of the same role before transmitting the payload to prevent 400 Bad Request errors.
• System Prompt Extraction: Hermes's system prompt must be cleanly separated from the main message array and mapped specifically to Google's systemInstruction parameter.
• Streaming Parity: Utilize Google's native streaming endpoint (stream=True) to properly yield text chunks to the Hermes TUI/WebUI while correctly pausing to buffer and parse tool argument streams.

### Alternatives Considered

OpenRouter: Works stably for Gemini tool calling right now, but adds a third-party dependency, potential latency, and requires users to manage a separate OpenRouter account instead of using their direct Google API keys.
• LiteLLM Local Proxy: Requires users to run and configure a separate local server to handle schema translation, adding unnecessary overhead and complexity to the basic setup process.
• Google's OpenAI Compatibility Endpoint: Currently too unstable for heavy multi-turn tool calling, often resulting in silent failures or dropped context during autonomous agent loops.

### Feature Type

CLI improvement

### Scope

Medium (few files, < 300 lines)

items.body:
## Summary

Currently, typing `/resume` inside the Hermes TUI/CLI without an argument either errors or prompts for an ID — but there's no way to *discover* that ID from within the session.

## The Problem

- `/resume <id>` works — but only if you already know the session ID
- Session IDs are opaque timestamp-based strings (e.g. `20260404_114702_bd197e`) with no in-session way to list them
- The official docs point users to `hermes --continue` / `hermes -c` from the terminal for resuming the last session — but that doesn't help when you're already inside a running session
- There's no in-TUI equivalent of the discoverability that `hermes -c` gives from the terminal

## Expected Behavior

`/resume` called with no arguments should open an interactive session picker — a scrollable list of recent sessions showing:
- Session title (or first message preview if untitled)
- Timestamp
- Source platform (cli / telegram / discord / etc.)
- Token count or rough size indicator

User picks one with arrow keys + Enter, and the session loads. Similar to how `fzf` or `prompt_toolkit`'s `radiolist_dialog` works.

## Proposed Implementation

The session data is already in SQLite (`~/.hermes/state.db`), so the picker just needs to query it:

```sql
SELECT session_id, title, source, started_at, total_tokens
FROM sessions
ORDER BY started_at DESC
LIMIT 20
```

Then render with `prompt_toolkit` (already a dependency) as an inline list or full-screen picker.

Fallback for non-interactive environments (piped input, Telegram, etc.): print the last 10 sessions as a numbered list and accept `/resume 3` style numeric selection.

## Why This Matters

- `/resume` is listed in `/help` but is effectively undiscoverable in practice — you have to `Ctrl+C` out, run a shell command to find the ID, then come back
- This is especially painful for Telegram/gateway users who can't easily run shell commands to look up IDs
- Related: #4528 (auto-output session ID on /new), #4059 (tab completion for slash commands)

## References

- Docs: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/sessions/#cli-session-resume
- Related issues: #4528, #4059

A user recently scanned this repo using [Qodo's AntiSlop Scanner](https://qodo.ai/ai-code-review-tool). The analysis reviewed 10 recent PRs and found **27 issues**, all confirmed to still exist on main.

Here's one example:

### Misattributed PID killing on MCP shutdown
**Severity:** action_required | **Category:** correctness

PID tracking in `_run_stdio` diffs child PID snapshots across an `async with stdio_client(...)` boundary while MCP servers are connected in parallel, so unrelated child PIDs can be captured and added to `_stdio_pids`. **How to validate:** Start multiple MCP servers in parallel via stdio transport, then trigger shutdown. Observe that PIDs from unrelated subprocesses appear in `_stdio_pids` and get killed.

**Agent prompt to fix:**
> In `_run_stdio`, track PIDs per-server instead of using a shared diff of all child PIDs. Associate each PID with its originating MCP server context so `_kill_orphaned_mcp_children()` only kills processes it actually spawned.

items.title: [Feature]: Allow delegate_task to accept provider/model parameters
items.body:
### Problem or Use Case

**Current Behavior**: 
The `delegate_task` tool schema includes `provider` and `model` parameters, but these are ignored in the handler implementation (`tools/delegate_tool.py` lines 403~581). Subagents always use the provider/model configured in `~/.hermes/config.yaml` under the `delegation:` section.

Current function signature:
```
def delegate_task(
    goal: Optional[str] = None,
    context: Optional[str] = None,
    toolsets: Optional[List[str]] = None,
    tasks: Optional[List[Dict[str, Any]]] = None,
    max_iterations: Optional[int] = None,
    parent_agent=None,
) -> str:
```

**Desired Behavior**:
Allow the `provider` and `model` parameters in `delegate_task` to override the global delegation configuration for that specific subagent call. This would enable:
- Orchestrators to spawn specialized subagents, i.e., vision models for image tasks, coding models for development, reasoning models for logic
- Per-task provider/model selection without changing global config
- Better resource utilization, i.e. use lower capacity model for small task, premium model for complex

**Use Cases**:
1. **Vision tasks**: Spawn subagent with vision capability (e.g. qwen/qwen2.5-vl-72b-instruct:free) for image analysis
2. **Voice tasks**: Use audio-optimized models for speech processing
3. **Mathematics/Logic**: Deploy reasoning-capable models for problem-solving
4. **Language tasks**: Use multilingual or language-specialized models (e.g. multilingual for translation )
5. **Cost optimization**: Route simple tasks to cheaper/free models, complex tasks to premium models

**Implementation Approach**:
Modify the `delegate_task` handler in `tools/delegate_tool.py` to:
1. Extract `provider` and `model` from `args` if provided
2. Pass these to the `_resolve_delegation_credentials()` function (or equivalent) 
3. Allow parameter-provided values to override config.yaml delegation settings
4. Maintain backward compatibility (when not provided, fallback to config.yaml)

**Related Code**:
- `tools/delegate_tool.py`: Handler function (lines 403~581)
- `_resolve_delegation_credentials()` function (lines ~583)
- Tool schema definition for `delegate_task`

This would transform delegation from a "one-size-fits-all" approach to a flexible per-task provider/model selection system while maintaining the existing config-based approach as fallback.

### Proposed Solution

Propose function signature:
```
def delegate_task(
    goal: Optional[str] = None,
    context: Optional[str] = None,
    toolsets: Optional[List[str]] = None,
    tasks: Optional[List[Dict[str, Any]]] = None,
    max_iterations: Optional[int] = None,
    provider: Optional[str] = None,        # Allow provider 
    model: Optional[str] = None,           # Allow model
    parent_agent=None,
) -> str:
```

As mentioned, the source of this information can be from:
- .env
- config.yaml
- agent's decision upon delegation (according to config.yaml)

items.title: Feature: in-session user progress updates via a dedicated tool
items.body:
## Summary

Hermes has `tool_progress` and a cross-platform `send_message` tool, but it does not have a simple way for the agent to send a natural-language update to the current user in the current session and then keep working.

This is useful for things like:
- an opening status update before work starts
- brief mid-task progress notes between tool calls
- user-facing updates that are clearer than raw tool previews, while keeping `tool_progress` available for auditability

## Problem

Today there are two nearby mechanisms, but neither solves this cleanly:
- `tool_progress` is machine-oriented and often exposes raw tool-call details rather than a concise user update
- `send_message` is for cross-channel delivery to an explicit target, not "message the current user in this session without ending the turn"

If the assistant sends a normal assistant message, the turn ends. That makes natural mid-turn progress updates awkward.

## Proposed behavior

Add a dedicated in-session tool for user-facing updates, something like `send_user_message(message=...)`, that:
- sends a short natural-language message to the current user in the current session/thread
- does not end the turn
- is available only in interactive runtimes where Hermes can actually route the message back to the user
- stays out of non-interactive surfaces like the OpenAI-compatible API server

This should be distinct from `send_message`, not a rename of it.

## Notes

This is complementary to richer UI/protocol work such as:
- interactive platform UX: #503
- RPC/protocol surfaces: #360
- ACP/editor integration: #569

The goal here is narrower: give the agent a simple, direct, natural-language progress-update primitive for normal Hermes sessions.

items.title: Feature: Configurable per-turn session flush to prevent data loss on force-exit

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Problem

When a user force-exits a CLI session (Ctrl+C × 2) during a long tool-calling chain, all messages since the last persist point are lost from `state.db`. The current implementation only calls `_persist_session()` / `_flush_messages_to_session_db()` on exit paths — after the full agent turn completes, on errors, or on InterruptedError. During normal operation within a turn, messages accumulate in memory with no intermediate writes to SQLite.

This means a 10-step tool chain that gets interrupted at step 8 loses all 8 steps, despite them having completed successfully. The JSON session logs (`~/.hermes/sessions/`) may partially capture this, but `state.db` — which powers `hermes -c`, `session_search`, and all session management — does not.

### Real-world scenario

User is in a CLI session with extensive tool-calling work. They accidentally hit Ctrl+C during a long-running tool (e.g., a `docker pull` with 120s timeout), then hit Ctrl+C again to force-exit before the InterruptedError handler fires. The entire session's tool call history since the last compression or turn boundary is gone from `state.db`. The session cannot be meaningfully resumed.

A significant contributing factor is **Ctrl+C muscle memory from GUI environments**. Users coming from Windows or macOS habitually use Ctrl+C as "copy" — and in a terminal context, that same keystroke sends SIGINT. For users who switch frequently between GUI applications and terminal sessions (which is most of us), accidental Ctrl+C hits during CLI work are not edge cases — they're a routine occurrence. A single accidental Ctrl+C interrupts the agent (recoverable), but a quick double-tap (natural when the first one "didn't seem to work") force-exits and drops all unflushed session state.

## Proposed solution

Add a configurable `flush_per_turn` option under the `compression:` config section that triggers `_flush_messages_to_session_db()` after each tool-call round and on no-tool-call (final) responses, before any branching logic.

### Config

```yaml
compression:
  flush_per_turn: false  # default: off (preserves existing behavior)
```

### Code changes

Two insertion points in `run_agent.py`, both gated on the config flag:

**1. Config read** (after `compression_protect_last`):
```python
self._flush_per_turn = str(_compression_cfg.get("flush_per_turn", False)).lower() in ("true", "1", "yes")
```

**2a. After tool-call execution** (after `_execute_tool_calls()` returns in the main loop):
```python
if self._flush_per_turn:
    self._flush_messages_to_session_db(messages, conversation_history)
```

**2b. On no-tool-call responses** (after `final_response = assistant_message.content or ""`):
```python
if self._flush_per_turn:
    self._flush_messages_to_session_db(messages, conversation_history)
```

### Why these two points

- **2a** covers the high-risk case: multi-step tool chains where a force-kill mid-chain loses all completed steps.
- **2b** covers plain responses. While the risk window here is tiny (the final `_persist_session` follows almost immediately), it costs nothing and provides belt-and-suspenders durability.
- The two paths are mutually exclusive (`if tool_calls` vs `else`), so there's no conflict.

### Why `compression:` section

The flush behavior is most closely related to session durability and context management, which is where `compression:` already lives. Alternative: a top-level `session:` or `persistence:` section, but that doesn't exist yet and this doesn't warrant creating one.

### Performance

`_flush_messages_to_session_db()` only writes messages added since `_last_flushed_db_idx`, so repeated calls are incremental — typically 1-3 INSERT statements per flush. SQLite is in WAL mode. Overhead is negligible.

### Default behavior

`false` — no change for anyone who doesn't opt in. Users who experience the data-loss scenario can enable it.

## Context

- Issue identified collaboratively by a user (Doc/@DocHogan) and Claude (Anthropic) during a debugging session where a force-exited CLI session lost its entire tool-call history from `state.db`.
- Related: #860 (duplicate-write bug that `_last_flushed_db_idx` was introduced to fix — this feature builds on that same cursor mechanism).
- Related: #886 (context compression silently dropping history — different vector, same category of silent data loss).

items.title: bug: `profile create --clone-all` copies entire infrastructure (~2.3GB) instead of just profile data

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Description

`hermes profile create --clone-all <name>` is extremely slow when cloning from the default profile (`~/.hermes`) because `shutil.copytree()` copies the **entire** directory tree with zero exclusions — including multi-GB infrastructure that is not profile data.

## Size breakdown of `~/.hermes`

| Directory | Size | Profile data? |
|-----------|------|---------------|
| `hermes-agent/` | **2.2 GB** | No (repo checkout) |
| ├── `venv/` | 680 MB | No (Python virtualenv) |
| ├── `node_modules/` | 167 MB | No (npm packages) |
| ├── `.git/` | 126 MB | No (git history) |
| `profiles/` | 21 MB | No (other profiles — recursive!) |
| `checkpoints/` | 16 MB | No (regenerable cache) |
| `state.db` | 11 MB | No (runtime database) |
| `bin/` | 9.4 MB | No (installed binaries) |
| `cache/` | 6.9 MB | No (regenerable) |
| **skills/** | **11 MB** | **Yes** |
| **sessions/** | **28 MB** | **Yes** |
| **memories/** | **12 KB** | **Yes** |
| **config.yaml, .env, SOUL.md, cron, etc.** | **~50 KB** | **Yes** |

**~2.26 GB of infrastructure is copied when only ~40 MB is actual profile data.**

## Root cause

In `hermes_cli/profiles.py` line 422:

```python
if clone_all and source_dir:
    shutil.copytree(source_dir, profile_dir)  # no ignore= parameter
```

## The fix already exists for export

`export_profile()` was fixed in commit 68fc4aec with `_DEFAULT_EXPORT_EXCLUDE_ROOT` (25+ entries) and `_default_export_ignore()` to exclude infrastructure from default profile exports. But `create_profile(clone_all=True)` was never updated to use the same exclusion logic.

## Expected behavior

`--clone-all` should copy all **profile state** (config, memories, sessions, skills, cron, plugins, .env, auth.json) but exclude infrastructure (hermes-agent repo, venv, node_modules, .git, databases, caches, other profiles).

## Documentation confirms this

All docs describe `--clone-all` as copying profile data, not infrastructure:

items.body:
## Description

When cron jobs (like beads pollers) find no work, agents are instructed to respond with `[SILENT]` — meaning nothing should be delivered to the user. However, LLMs often add preamble text (e.g. "No open issues assigned to me.") before or alongside `[SILENT]`, causing nearly-empty but still-delivered messages in chat.

This affects any cron job that uses `[SILENT]` as a "no output" signal.

## Proposed Solution

Add platform-level suppression in Hermes: when a cron job response contains `[SILENT]` as its only meaningful content, skip delivery entirely. The filter should:

1. Check if the response, stripped of whitespace, equals `[SILENT]` exactly
2. Optionally, also suppress responses where `[SILENT]` is the only substantive content (with possible minor preamble)
3. Log the suppression so it's visible in cron job logs but never reaches the user's chat

## Workaround

Currently worked around by adding explicit "output ONLY [SILENT]" instructions in cron prompts, but this is redundant when the same rule already exists in SOUL.md and LLMs are unreliable at following zero-output instructions.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent (latest)
- Cron job delivery to Discord
- Multiple agent profiles affected

items.title: fix: DingTalk platform adapter has multiple bugs preventing message processing
items.body:
## Description

The DingTalk platform adapter (`gateway/platforms/dingtalk.py`) has several critical bugs that prevent it from receiving and responding to messages. Found while debugging on HarmonyOS 4 (DingTalk mobile client).

## Bugs Found

### 1. `DingTalkStreamClient.start` wrapped incorrectly with `asyncio.to_thread`

**Line 135 (original):**
```python
await asyncio.to_thread(self._stream_client.start)
```

`DingTalkStreamClient.start()` is an async coroutine. `asyncio.to_thread()` is designed for synchronous (blocking) functions — wrapping an async function creates a coroutine object that never gets awaited. This causes repeated reconnection loops with no useful error.

**Fix:** Changed to `await self._stream_client.start()`

### 2. `process()` method signature mismatch with SDK base class

The `dingtalk_stream.ChatbotHandler.process()` is defined as `async def process(self, message: CallbackMessage)` in the SDK. The adapter overrides it as a regular `def process(self, message)` — when the SDK tries `await handler.process(message)`, it gets a plain tuple `(STATUS_OK, "OK")` and fails with:

```
ERROR dingtalk_stream.client: error processing message: object tuple can't be used in 'await' expression
```

**Fix:** Changed to `async def process(self, message)` and replaced blocking `future.result(timeout=60)` with fire-and-forget `future.add_done_callback()` for error logging.

### 3. `TimeoutError` from blocking `future.result(timeout=60)`

The `process()` method blocked the dingtalk-stream SDK thread waiting for agent processing to complete within 60 seconds. Agent responses typically take longer (tool calls, LLM inference), causing a `TimeoutError` and preventing the ACK from being returned to the SDK promptly.

```
ERROR gateway.platforms.dingtalk: [DingTalk] Error processing incoming message
TimeoutError
```

**Fix:** Return ACK immediately, dispatch agent work as fire-and-forget background task.

### 4. `_extract_text()` fails on `CallbackMessage` — messages silently dropped

The SDK sends messages as `CallbackMessage` with all fields inside `message.data` dict (e.g., `message.data['text'] = {'content': 'hello'}`). The adapter uses `getattr(message, "text", None)` which returns `None` since `CallbackMessage` has no `text` attribute — only `data`, `headers`, `spec_version`, `type`, `extensions`.

Result: text extraction returns empty string, message is silently skipped with DEBUG log `"Empty message, skipping"`.

**Fix:** Added fallback to `message.data['text']['content']` for `CallbackMessage` format.

### 5. `_on_message()` fails to extract any fields from `CallbackMessage`

Same issue as #4 but for ALL fields: `conversation_id`, `sender_id`, `sender_nick`, `sender_staff_id`, `session_webhook`, `create_at`, `conversation_title`. All use `getattr(message, "...", default)` which returns defaults since `CallbackMessage` stores everything in `data` dict with camelCase keys (`conversationId`, `senderId`, `sessionWebhook`, etc.).

Result: `session_webhook` is never captured, replies cannot be sent. User IDs are empty, authorization fails.

**Fix:** Added `_get_field()` helper with `_DATA_KEY_MAP` (snake_case to camelCase) that falls back to `message.data[key]`.

### 6. Authorization uses unreadable encrypted `senderId` instead of `senderStaffId`

DingTalk provides two user identifiers:
- `senderId`: encrypted open ID like `$:LWCP_v1:$qoM1+WxS0Q5F5iqeTKOz7Hge06B2HTXW` (unreadable, varies per app)
- `senderStaffId`: numeric corp employee ID like `22514138787330` (human-readable, stable)

The adapter used `senderId` as `user_id` for authorization, making it impractical to add users to allowlists.

**Fix:** Use `senderStaffId` as primary `user_id`, keep `senderId` as `user_id_alt`.

## Environment

- **OS:** HarmonyOS 4 (DingTalk mobile client sending messages)
- **Hermes:** Current `cli` branch
- **Python:** 3.11.15
- **dingtalk-stream SDK:** Latest from pip
- **Platform:** DingTalk Stream Mode (WebSocket)

## Reproduction

1. Configure DingTalk platform in `config.yaml`
2. Start gateway: `hermes gateway run`
3. Send message from DingTalk mobile client
4. Observe: messages arrive but are silently dropped or timeout

## Fixes Applied

All six bugs have been fixed locally. The changes ensure:
- Stream client starts correctly with `await`
- SDK thread is not blocked by long-running agent processing
- `CallbackMessage` fields are properly extracted via `data` dict
- Human-readable staff IDs are used for authorization

Happy to submit a PR if the fixes look good.

items.title: Message handling behavior when multiple messages arrive during active agent execution
items.body:
## Summary
When a user sends multiple messages in quick succession while an agent is still processing a previous message, several observable behaviors occur that create a confusing user experience. I would like to understand the intended design and whether these behaviors are expected or represent areas for improvement.

## Observed Behaviors

### 1. Message Content Replacement (Not Queueing)
**Observation:** When message B arrives while message A is being processed, message A's content appears to be replaced/discarded, and only message B is processed.

**Expected vs Actual:**
- User expectation: Both messages would be processed sequentially (FIFO)
- Actual behavior: Only the most recent message is processed

**Question:** Is the intended design that new messages should interrupt and replace pending ones, rather than queueing? This creates data loss from the user's perspective.

---

### 2. Response References Wrong Message (Confirmed Bug)
**Observation:** In some cases, the agent's response appears to reference message A (the first message) while actually answering message B (the second message), or vice versa. The context seems to get mismatched.

**Example:**
- User sends: "Check the weather in New York"
- User sends (3 seconds later): "Check the weather in Los Angeles"
- Agent responds about Los Angeles weather but the reply context/threading suggests it's responding to the New York message

This appears to be a bug where the message context/metadata gets out of sync with the actual content being processed.

---

### 3. Task Termination Behavior is Unclear
**Observation:** When a new message arrives during active processing, it's unclear whether the previous task:
- Is immediately terminated (hard stop)
- Continues running to completion despite the interrupt signal
- Is gracefully wound down at the next checkpoint

From the user's perspective, long-running operations (e.g., terminal commands, file searches) appear to continue even after sending a new message, creating confusion about whether the interrupt actually worked.

**Question:** What is the intended termination semantics? Should users expect immediate cancellation, or is the cooperative interruption model the explicit design choice?

---

## Design Intent Questions

1. **Interrupt vs Queue Philosophy:** Is the design intentionally "last message wins" (LIFO) rather than FIFO? If so, would it be helpful to notify users when a message is being replaced rather than silently dropping it?

2. **Preemptive vs Cooperative Interruption:** The code shows `_interrupt_requested` flags being checked at various checkpoints. Was this cooperative model chosen to prevent data corruption (e.g., half-written files), or would a more aggressive termination model be considered?

3. **UX for Message Replacement:** Would you be open to a notification like "⏹️ Previous task cancelled, processing new request..." so users understand their first message was dropped?

## Context
This was observed when using the Telegram integration, where users naturally send follow-up messages before receiving responses (especially during long-running operations). The current behavior feels contradictory:
- The system accepts new input immediately
- But it silently drops previous input
- And may still complete the previous operation anyway
- While referencing the wrong original message

Would appreciate clarification on which behaviors are intentional vs potential issues to address.

---
**Environment:**
- Platform: Telegram
- hermes-agent version: Latest main branch (as of 2025-01)

items.body:
### Bug Description


**Affects:** v2026.4.3 (commit 77a2aad7)
**Models:** Kimi K2.5, GLM-5, Qwen (via Ollama)

## Summary

Models served through Ollama can return invalid surrogate code points (U+D800-U+DFFF) that crash `json.dumps()` during UTF-8 serialization. This causes a `UnicodeEncodeError` that retries 3 times and then fails completely.

```
API call failed after 3 retries: 'utf-8' codec can't encode characters in position 45559-45560: surrogates not allowed
    Model: glm-5:cloud
```

### Steps to Reproduce


1. Set up Hermes with an Ollama-hosted model (Kimi K2.5, GLM-5, or Qwen)
2. Configure the model in config.yaml  
3. Trigger a large payload that may contain surrogate characters in:
   - File read operations with binary-like content
   - Long tool outputs or session history
   - Any content where the model's response contains lone surrogates
4. The API call will fail with UnicodeEncodeError, retry 3 times, and crash

**Minimal reproduction:**

 
# In Hermes CLI with glm-5:cloud or kimi-k2.5:cloud via Ollama:
hermes

# Ask the model to process a file or have a long conversation
# that produces a response with surrogate characters:

> read a large binary-adjacent file and summarize it
# OR
> continue a long session where history contains surrogates

# Error appears:
# API call failed after 3 retries: 'utf-8' codec can't encode
# characters in position XXXXX-XXXXX: surrogates not allowed

**Why it reproduces intermittently:** Surrogates appear in model outputs unpredictably. Some Ollama models occasionally emit them when processing certain content. The position number (e.g., 45559) indicates where in the serialized JSON payload the surrogates occur.




### Expected Behavior

Commands should be processed.

### Actual Behavior

API call failed after 3 retries: 'utf-8' codec can't encode characters in position 45559-45560: surrogates not allowed

..and it doesn't process the command.

### Affected Component

CLI (interactive chat), Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Operating System

macOS 26.2

### Python Version

Python 3.11.15

### Hermes Version

0.7.0 (2026.4.3)

### Relevant Logs / Traceback

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

Models served through Ollama can return invalid surrogate code points (U+D800-U+DFFF) that crash `json.dumps()` during UTF-8 serialization. This causes a `UnicodeEncodeError` that retries 3 times and then fails completely.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

## Fix (3 call sites)

### 1. Add proactive sanitization before API call (line ~6823)

Insert after `_sanitize_api_messages()`:

```python
            api_messages = self._sanitize_api_messages(api_messages)

            # Proactive surrogate sanitization: clean any lone surrogates from
            # tool results, session history, or other sources before API call.
            # Prevents UnicodeEncodeError during json.dumps() serialization.
            _sanitize_messages_surrogates(api_messages)

            # Calculate approximate request size for logging
```

### 2. Sanitize API responses before storing (line ~5242)

Replace:

```python
        msg = {
            "role": "assistant",
            "content": assistant_message.content or "",
            "reasoning": reasoning_text,
            "finish_reason": finish_reason,
        }
```

With:

        raw_content = assistant_message.content or ""
        sanitized_content = _sanitize_surrogates(raw_content)
        if reasoning_text:
            reasoning_text = _sanitize_surrogates(reasoning_text)

        msg = {
            "role": "assistant",
            "content": sanitized_content,
            "reasoning": reasoning_text,
            "finish_reason": finish_reason,
        }
```

### 3. Fix retry path (line ~7336)

```python
# Change:
if _sanitize_messages_surrogates(messages):

# To:
if _sanitize_messages_surrogates(api_messages):
```

items.title: feat(matrix): add auto_thread support for group rooms
items.body:
## Problem

When the Matrix bot responds in a group room, its replies go directly into the main room timeline. In busy rooms this causes context bleed between conversations and clutters the timeline for other participants.

Discord already solves this with `DISCORD_AUTO_THREAD`, which automatically creates a thread for each bot interaction so conversations stay isolated.

## Proposed Solution

Add `MATRIX_AUTO_THREAD` support for the Matrix adapter, mirroring Discord's `DISCORD_AUTO_THREAD`.

**Behavior:**
- **Group rooms** (when `MATRIX_AUTO_THREAD=true`): Bot responses are sent as threaded replies (MSC3440 `m.thread` relation) to the original message, implicitly creating a thread
- **Existing threads**: No change — the bot already replies within the thread
- **DMs**: No threading applied
- Threads created by auto-thread are tracked for participation, so `MATRIX_REQUIRE_MENTION` is bypassed in those threads

**Configuration:**
```bash
# .env
MATRIX_AUTO_THREAD=true   # default: true
```

Or in `config.yaml`:
```yaml
matrix:
  auto_thread: true
```

## Context

Discord implements this pattern — see `DISCORD_AUTO_THREAD` in `gateway/platforms/discord.py`. The Matrix implementation is simpler since Matrix threads are implicit (just a relation type on a message), requiring no API call to "create" a thread.

This is a companion feature to `MATRIX_REQUIRE_MENTION` (#3891) — together they bring Matrix to feature parity with Discord's conversation management.

items.title: Honcho plugin: race condition in session cache causes silent conclusion/memory loss
items.body:
## Bug Description

`create_conclusion()` in the Honcho plugin intermittently fails with no error propagated to the user. The root cause is a race condition between the `sync_turn` background thread and the main thread accessing `HonchoSessionManager._cache` (a plain `dict`) without any synchronization.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Enable Honcho memory plugin with `writeFrequency: "async"`
2. Make rapid consecutive `honcho_conclude` tool calls (e.g., 10+ in a row)
3. Some calls return `"Failed to save conclusion"` at random positions
4. Retrying the exact same text succeeds (timing-dependent)
5. Direct Honcho SDK calls work fine for the same content

## Root Cause

**`_cache` in `session.py:94` is an unprotected `dict` accessed from multiple threads:**

- **Main thread** (tool calls): `handle_tool_call` → `create_conclusion` → `self._cache.get(session_key)` (session.py:916)
- **Background thread** (`sync_turn`): spawned at `__init__.py:569`, calls `self._manager.get_or_create(self._session_key)` (line 559) which reads/writes `_cache`
- **Background thread** (`on_memory_write`): spawned at `__init__.py:589`, calls `create_conclusion` which reads `_cache`

`get_or_create()` is not atomic — it checks membership, creates objects, then assigns to `_cache` (session.py:234-284). If the sync thread is mid-operation, the main thread's `_cache.get()` can miss the entry.

While CPython's GIL makes individual dict operations atomic, the multi-step read-modify-write in `get_or_create()` is not protected, leading to intermittent cache misses.

## Impact

**High** — silent knowledge loss. Conclusions (user facts, preferences, corrections) are dropped without any indication to the user. This also affects:
- `on_memory_write()` which mirrors built-in memory writes as conclusions (same race)
- `sync_turn()` which records conversation turns
- Any operation depending on `_cache.get(session_key)` succeeding

This undermines the core value proposition of the Honcho plugin as a long-term memory provider.

## Proposed Fix

Add a `threading.Lock` to protect `_cache` access in `HonchoSessionManager`:

```python
# session.py __init__
self._cache_lock = threading.Lock()

# All _cache reads/writes wrapped:
with self._cache_lock:
    if key in self._cache:
        return self._cache[key]
```

Alternatively, join the `sync_thread` before processing tool calls in `handle_tool_call()`.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.7.0
- honcho-ai SDK (latest)
- Gateway mode (Telegram platform)
- `writeFrequency: "async"` in honcho.json

1. Extract the file path from the response text

3. Deliver the file as an attachment via `send_image()` or `send_document()`

- `gateway/platforms/signal.py` - Signal adapter with working attachment methods
- `gateway/platforms/base.py` - Base adapter with `cache_image_from_bytes()`, `cache_image_from_url()` utilities
- `tests/gateway/test_send_image_file.py` - Tests for MEDIA: tag parsing

- Signal adapter using signal-cli HTTP daemon
- Gateway expects `SIGNAL_HTTP_URL` and `SIGNAL_ACCOUNT` env vars

items.body:
## Problem
On macOS, `hermes gateway start` can create a second local gateway process when the launchd plist needs refreshing.

## Root cause
`refresh_launchd_plist_if_needed()` unloads and reloads the launchd plist. Because the plist also has `RunAtLoad`, the reload already starts the gateway again. `launchd_start()` then unconditionally calls `launchctl start`, which can race a second local gateway process into existence.

## Impact
That duplicate local process can grab Telegram/Discord/WhatsApp scoped locks and produce self-conflicts like:
- Telegram polling conflicts / token lock
- Discord token already in use
- WhatsApp session already in use

## Suggested fix
If the plist was refreshed via unload+load, return early from `launchd_start()` instead of issuing a second explicit `launchctl start`.

items.title: bug: delegate_task subagent sessions pollute session list as orphan entries
items.body:
## Description

When `delegate_task` spawns subagent sessions, they appear in `hermes sessions list` and `/resume` as untitled orphan entries indistinguishable from real user sessions.

## Root Cause

`delegate_tool.py` passes `session_db` to child agents (line 229) but not `parent_session_id`. The child agent calls `create_session()` (run_agent.py:968) with `parent_session_id=None`, creating a top-level session with `source=cli`.

The DB schema already has `parent_session_id` as a FK column on the sessions table, and `session_search` already handles it correctly (filters children in recent list, resolves to parent in FTS). But `delegate_tool` never wires it up.

## Reproduction

```
hermes chat
> delegate a task to check the date
> /resume
```

The subagent session appears as an untitled entry alongside real sessions.

## Impact

- `hermes sessions list` shows orphan subagent sessions
- `/resume` picker shows them
- `session_search` recent sessions list shows them
- Each `delegate_task` call (especially batch with 3 tasks) creates 1-3 extra visible sessions

## Additional: FK cascade bug in delete_session/prune_sessions

The `sessions.parent_session_id` FK has no `ON DELETE CASCADE`. When sessions DO have `parent_session_id` set (compression chains today, subagents after fix), deleting a parent raises `IntegrityError` because children reference it.

`delete_session()` and `prune_sessions()` need to delete children before parents.

## Suggested Fix

1. Pass `parent_session_id=parent_agent.session_id` in `delegate_tool._build_child_agent()`
2. Add `parent_session_id` param to `run_agent.py` `__init__`, pass to `create_session()`
3. Filter `parent_session_id IS NULL` in `list_sessions_rich()`
4. Delete children first in `delete_session()`/`prune_sessions()`

items.title: `hermes gateway restart` hangs on macOS due to KeepAlive race condition

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Problem
`hermes gateway restart` hangs indefinitely on macOS when the gateway is managed by launchd with `KeepAlive/SuccessfulExit = false`.

## Root cause
`launchd_restart()` in `hermes_cli/gateway.py` does:
1. `launchctl stop <label>` — sends SIGTERM
2. `_wait_for_gateway_exit()` — polls until the PID disappears
3. `launchctl start <label>`

But with `KeepAlive/SuccessfulExit = false`, launchd immediately respawns the process after stop, so step 2 never completes — the old PID dies but a new one appears instantly.

## Fix
Use `launchctl kickstart -kp gui/<uid>/<label>` which atomically kills and restarts the service in one operation, avoiding the race. Falls back to the old stop/wait/start sequence if kickstart fails (e.g., on older macOS).

## Environment
- macOS (tested on M4 Max, Sequoia)
- launchd plist with KeepAlive/SuccessfulExit = false

items.title: bug: call_llm() has no retry on transient failures
items.body:
## Description

`call_llm()` in `agent/auxiliary_client.py` (line ~1661) makes a single API call with zero retry on transient failures (HTTP 429, 5xx, timeouts). Every failure silently discards the operation.

## Impact

Affects **all** auxiliary LLM consumers:
- Vision analysis
- Context compression
- Skills hub
- Memory extraction (hermes-v2 plugin)
- Memory consolidation
- Session search summarization
- Any future `call_llm()` consumer

A single network hiccup or rate limit causes the entire operation to fail silently. For memory extraction, the next attempt is 8+ turns away. For compression, the context window fills up without recovery.

## Proposed Fix

Add a single retry with exponential backoff for transient errors inside `call_llm()`:
- Retry on: `429`, `500`, `502`, `503`, `504`, `httpx.ConnectError`, `httpx.TimeoutException`
- Max 1 retry, 2-second backoff
- No retry on: `400`, `401`, `403`, `404` (client errors that won't self-resolve)

The retry belongs in `call_llm()` itself (not in individual callers) so all consumers benefit uniformly.

## Related

- #5048 (fixes other memory provider integration bugs found during the same review)
- #5129 (background review double-loads provider — same audit)

items.body:
## Description

The background memory review (run_agent.py ~line 1680) spawns a full AIAgent clone to review conversation history. This clone creates its own `_memory_manager` which loads the configured memory provider a second time. For providers backed by local databases (hermes-v2, holographic), this creates a second engine instance pointing at the same SQLite file.

## Impact

- Two extraction engines running independently against the same DB
- Duplicate memories possible (both engines extract from overlapping message windows)
- Two consolidation passes possible at session end
- Doubled resource usage (connections, caches, embedding models)
- Affects any memory plugin that creates expensive local resources during `initialize()`

SQLite WAL mode prevents corruption, so this is a correctness issue (duplicates) not a safety issue (data loss).

## Proposed Fix

Pass the parent agent's `_memory_manager` to the review agent instead of letting it auto-create:

```python
# In the review agent construction (~line 1687):
review_agent._memory_manager = self._memory_manager  # share, don't duplicate
```

Or add a `memory_manager` kwarg to AIAgent.`__init__()` that, when provided, skips the auto-load path.

This requires careful consideration since AIAgent is constructed from CLI, gateway, cron, delegation, and subagent paths — the constructor signature change needs to be tested across all callers.

## Related

- #5048 (fixes other memory provider integration bugs found during the same review)
- #5128 (call_llm no retry — same audit)

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Bug Description
When running `hermes status` from an SSH session where the systemd user D-Bus is not accessible, the gateway status incorrectly reports "stopped" even when the gateway is actively running.

## Environment
- VPS (OVH), Linux, SSH session
- hermes v2026.4.3

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Connect via SSH to the VPS
2. Run `hermes status`
3. Observe: Gateway Service → Status: ✗ stopped
4. Meanwhile `hermes gateway status` shows: active (running)

## Root Cause
The status check relies solely on `systemctl --user is-active`. When that command fails (e.g. "Failed to connect to bus: No medium found" in SSH sessions without user D-Bus), `is_active` stays False. No fallback mechanism exists.

## Fix
Added `_fallback_gateway_check()` that reads the PID file (`~/.hermes/gateway.pid`) and verifies the process exists using `os.kill(pid, 0)`. Falls back to this check when systemctl returns non-active.

## Files Modified
- `hermes_cli/status.py` — added `_fallback_gateway_check()` function and fallback logic in the Linux systemd check block

labels.name: comp/cli

items.body:
## Description

Pressing `Ctrl+C` during slow slash commands (e.g., `/skills browse`) terminates the entire CLI session instead of interrupting the command and returning to the input prompt.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start `hermes` in interactive mode
2. Run a slow slash command: `/skills browse`
3. Press `Ctrl+C` while the command is still loading

## Expected Behavior

The slash command is interrupted and the user is returned to the input prompt (same as interrupting an agent mid-task with a normal prompt).

## Actual Behavior

The entire CLI session exits and returns to the shell. The session may not be saved to `state.db`, making `hermes -c` unable to resume.

## Root Cause

Slash commands are handled outside the agent loop (e.g., `_handle_skills_command()` → `hermes_cli/skills_hub.py`). The `KeyboardInterrupt` from `Ctrl+C` is not caught in this path, so it propagates to the outermost `except (EOFError, KeyboardInterrupt, BrokenPipeError): pass` in `cli.py` (around line 8011), which silently exits the session.

In contrast, `Ctrl+C` during agent execution is caught within `run_agent.py`'s agent loop, properly interrupting the current task and returning to the input prompt.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent (latest `main`)
- Terminal: SSH session (Ghostty on Mac → VPS)

items.title: UX: streaming retry status messages accumulate in chat thread even after successful retry

labels.name: comp/agent

labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Problem

When a streaming request to the LLM provider fails mid-stream (e.g. `RemoteProtocolError`, `ConnectionError`, backend 502), Hermes correctly retries with a fresh connection. Each retry attempt emits a status message to the user via `_emit_status()`:

```
⚠️ Connection to provider dropped (RemoteProtocolError). Reconnecting… (attempt 2/3)
⚠️ Connection to provider dropped (RemoteProtocolError). Reconnecting… (attempt 3/3)
```

These messages are sent to the user-facing channel (Slack, Telegram, etc.) and **remain in the conversation thread permanently**, even when the final retry succeeds. On a self-hosted provider where transient errors can happen several times in an hour (backend restarts, rate limits, OOM recovery), the channel accumulates retry warnings that don't reflect the actual outcome of the request.

## What the user sees in Slack today

```
user: look up a PR to work on
alfred: ⚠️ Connection to provider dropped (RemoteProtocolError). Reconnecting… (attempt 2/3)
alfred: ⚠️ Connection to provider dropped (RemoteProtocolError). Reconnecting… (attempt 3/3)
alfred: <the actual successful response>
```

When retries eventually succeed, the two warning messages are noise. When they fail, the final `❌ Connection to provider failed after N attempts` is useful on its own.

## Source

`run_agent.py` around line 4365 (inside the streaming retry loop):

```python
if _stream_attempt < _max_stream_retries:
    logger.info("Streaming attempt %s/%s failed ...", ...)
    self._emit_status(
        f"⚠️ Connection to provider dropped "
        f"({type(e).__name__}). Reconnecting… "
        f"(attempt {_stream_attempt + 2}/{_max_stream_retries + 1})"
    )
```

`_emit_status()` sends directly to the platform adapter, which in most platforms posts a new message (not an update to an existing message).

## Suggested behaviors

Any of these would be an improvement:

**1. Silent retry on success.** Don't emit per-retry warnings unless the final outcome is a failure. The final `❌ Connection to provider failed after N attempts` already conveys the failure case.

**2. Ephemeral status messages that are replaced, not appended.** Use platform-specific edit/update primitives:
- Slack: `chat.update` on a single status message, or use ephemeral messages
- Telegram: edit the same message rather than posting new ones
- CLI: overwrite the same terminal line with `\r`

The adapter layer would need a `_emit_status_transient()` variant that edits in place.

**3. Downgrade to logger-only for intermediate retries.** Only surface the FINAL outcome to the user. Intermediate attempts go to `logger.info` / `logger.warning` and stay in logs. This is the simplest change — remove the `_emit_status()` call from the retry branch and rely on the already-present `logger.info()`.

## Why this matters

For self-hosters running local inference backends, transient errors are more common than with hosted APIs (OOMs during model swaps, backend restarts via launchd/systemd, service recovery windows). A session that successfully completes 10 turns but had 3 transient retries accumulates 6 warning messages that aren't actionable. Agentic workflows with many tool calls multiply this.

For hosted API users, rate-limit retries also generate these messages on every spike.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent (current main as of 2026-04-04)
- Slack gateway (Socket Mode)
- Self-hosted LLM backend (observed with vMLX + blockops-proxy returning 502s during Metal OOM recovery)

items.title: OPENAI_BASE_URL env var not cleared on provider switch — silently poisons auxiliary clients
items.body:
Hermes version: v0.7.0 (2026.4.3)
OS: Ubuntu 24 / WSL2
Python: 3.11.14

What happened
Switching providers via hermes model (from a custom endpoint back to OpenRouter) correctly updates config.yaml with the new base_url and provider, but leaves any pre-existing OPENAI_BASE_URL value in ~/.hermes/.env untouched.
In my case: I had previously configured Hermes to use NVIDIA's inference endpoint (https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1/) via OPENAI_BASE_URL in .env. When I later switched back to OpenRouter via hermes model, the main inference client worked correctly because it uses the explicit base_url from config.yaml. However, auxiliary clients (compression, vision, subagent delegation) that are initialized with provider: auto fell back to OPENAI_BASE_URL from the environment and were silently routing to NVIDIA.
Why it's hard to diagnose
The failure is asymmetric. Main conversations succeed (correct routing). Compression triggers at context thresholds and hits the wrong endpoint -- producing silent failures or degraded output. Subagents via delegate_task hit the wrong endpoint and fail mysteriously. The symptoms look like intermittent model quality issues or random task failures, not a configuration problem.
The auto-remediation system (retry/fallback cascade) doesn't catch it because the errors occur on code paths that don't feed back into the main inference error handler.
Steps to reproduce

Set OPENAI_BASE_URL=https://some-custom-endpoint.example.com/v1 in ~/.hermes/.env
Run hermes model and switch to OpenRouter with a standard model
Confirm config.yaml shows correct base_url: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1
Start a long session that triggers context compression
Compression auxiliary client routes to the custom endpoint, not OpenRouter

Expected behavior
When hermes model switches to a named provider (openrouter, nous, anthropic, etc.), OPENAI_BASE_URL in .env should either be removed or commented out if it conflicts with the new configuration. At minimum, Hermes should warn at startup when OPENAI_BASE_URL is set in the environment but doesn't match the base_url in config.yaml.
Proposed fix
A startup check along these lines:
pythonenv_base_url = os.environ.get("OPENAI_BASE_URL")
config_base_url = config.get("model", {}).get("base_url")
if env_base_url and config_base_url and env_base_url.rstrip("/") != config_base_url.rstrip("/"):
    logger.warning(
        f"OPENAI_BASE_URL={env_base_url!r} is set in your environment but conflicts with "
        f"base_url={config_base_url!r} in config.yaml. Auxiliary clients may route to the "
        f"wrong endpoint. Comment out OPENAI_BASE_URL in ~/.hermes/.env to resolve."
    )
Alternatively, hermes model could scrub OPENAI_BASE_URL from .env when switching to a named provider that has its own base_url, mirroring what it already does for api_mode.

Additional context
The hermes doctor command does not currently check for this conflict. Adding it to the doctor checks would also catch the problem before it causes confusing behavior.

### Summary

When running `hermes claw migrate` on an existing OpenClaw installation, the migration moves `~/.openclaw/` to `~/.openclaw.pre-migration-YYYYMMDD/` as a backup — but does **not** copy `openclaw.json` to the new `~/.openclaw/` directory.

The result: the new gateway starts with no config file. It has no auth token, no model credentials, and no channel configuration. The failure mode is silent and confusing.

### Symptoms

- Gateway starts but agent immediately crashes with:
  ```
  ENOENT: no such file or directory, chdir '/home/user/.openclaw.pre-migration-YYYYMMDD/workspace' -> '/home/user/.openclaw/workspace'
  ```
- `openclaw logs` shows: `unauthorized: gateway token missing`
- `openclaw status` reports gateway unreachable

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Have a working OpenClaw installation with `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`
2. Run `hermes claw migrate`
3. Observe that `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json` does not exist post-migration
4. Gateway starts blind

### Fix / Workaround

```bash
cp ~/.openclaw.pre-migration/openclaw.json ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json
systemctl --user restart openclaw-gateway
```

Additionally, `~/.hermes/.env` won't have Slack tokens — they need to be manually extracted from the restored `openclaw.json` and added:

echo 'SLACK_BOT_TOKEN=xoxb-...' >> ~/.hermes/.env
echo 'SLACK_APP_TOKEN=xapp-...' >> ~/.hermes/.env
hermes gateway install
hermes gateway start
```

### Expected Behavior

`hermes claw migrate` should either:
1. Copy `openclaw.json` to the new `~/.openclaw/` location (preferred), or
2. Emit a clear warning that the config was not migrated and provide the copy command

Silent failure with a cryptic `chdir` error is very hard to debug.

If `hermes gateway run` is configured with multiple messaging platforms (e.g. Slack + Mattermost) and any single platform fails to connect, the gateway exits with an error instead of running with the remaining connected platforms.

items.body:
# GitHub Issue: Feature — Script/shell execution as cron job action

## Title
`Feature: Script/shell execution as cron job action (alternative to LLM agent)`

## Body

### Problem

Currently every Hermes cron job spawns an `AIAgent` instance, even when the job's purpose is a simple conditional check. A common pattern is using a cron job to poll for work (e.g. beads-poller) where the agent must respond with `[SILENT]` when there's nothing to do.

This has two problems:
1. **Cost** — the LLM runs and consumes tokens on every tick, even when there's no work
2. **Reliability** — asking an LLM to produce *exactly* `[SILENT]` and nothing else is fighting against how they work. Agents frequently output extra text around `[SILENT]`, breaking the suppression mechanism

### Proposal

Add a new `type` field to cron jobs (defaulting to the current `agent` behavior):

```yaml
# Current behavior (unchanged)
type: agent
prompt: "Check beads and do work if found"

# New: script execution — no LLM involved
type: script
script: ~/.hermes/scripts/beads-poller-hawk.sh
```

**Key behaviors for `type: script`:**
- Hermes executes the script file in a shell subprocess — no `AIAgent` is created
- The script must be an existing file on disk (absolute or relative to `HERMES_HOME`)
- Exit code 0 with stdout containing `[SILENT]` → suppress delivery (same as current agent behavior)
- Exit code 0 with other output → deliver stdout as the cron result
- Exit code non-zero → deliver stderr as error
- Environment variables available: `HERMES_HOME`, plus any from the profile's `.env`

### Why not just use a system crontab?

You *can* — but that means:
- Moving work scheduling out of Hermes entirely
- Losing the centralized `hermes cron list` management view
- Needing Discord webhook URLs or Hermes webhook endpoints to trigger the agent through its gateway
- Per-profile system crontab entries instead of one unified system

Keeping script execution *inside* Hermes cron preserves the management UX while eliminating the unnecessary LLM invocation.

### Example use cases

1. **Beads polling** — check `bd ready`, only trigger agent if work exists
2. **Health checks** — run a script, only page if something's wrong
3. **External service polling** — curl an API, only trigger agent on status change

items.title: Bug: OpenCode Go model names with dots get hyphenated, causing HTTP 401 (minimax-m2.7, glm-4.5, kimi-k2.5)
items.body:
## Summary

When using the `opencode-go` provider with the Hermes Agent CLI, any model whose name contains a dot as a version separator (e.g. `minimax-m2.7`, `glm-4.5`, `kimi-k2.5`) is silently mangled before the API request is made — dots are replaced with hyphens. This causes the OpenCode Go endpoint to return HTTP 401:

```
error type: ModelError
message: Model minimax-m2-7 not supported
```

The root cause is **not** the OpenCode Go API itself. Manual `curl` requests with the correct model name (`minimax-m2.7`) succeed. The bug lives entirely inside Hermes and affects two separate code paths.

---

## Affected Models (non-exhaustive)

| Model | Mangled to | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `minimax-m2.7` | `minimax-m2-7` | 401 from OpenCode Go |
| `minimax-m2.5` | `minimax-m2-5` | 401 from OpenCode Go |
| `glm-4.5` | `glm-4-5` | 401 from OpenCode Go |
| `kimi-k2.5` | `kimi-k2-5` | 401 from OpenCode Go |
| `mimo-v2-omni` | `mimo-v2-omni` | Works (no dot, coincidence) |
| `glm-5` | `glm-5` | Works (no dot, coincidence) |

Models without a `.` version separator appeared to work not because the logic was correct, but because the mangled output happens to match the input.

---

## Root Cause — Two Separate Bugs

### Bug 1: `hermes/cli/model_normalize.py` — `opencode-go` incorrectly in `DOT_TO_HYPHEN_PROVIDERS`

`opencode-go` was included in `DOT_TO_HYPHEN_PROVIDERS` (alongside `anthropic`), causing `normalize_model_for_provider()` to call `dots_to_hyphens()` on all model names for this provider. The Anthropic API uses hyphens (e.g. `claude-sonnet-4-6`), but OpenCode Go uses its own identifiers with dots (e.g. `minimax-m2.7`).

**Fix:**
```diff
 DOT_TO_HYPHEN_PROVIDERS: frozenset[str] = frozenset({
     "anthropic",
     "opencode-zen",
-    "opencode-go",
 })
```

### Bug 2: `run_agent.py` — `anthropic_preserve_dots()` missing `opencode-go`

When the API mode is `anthropic_messages` (which MiniMax models on the Go endpoint use), Hermes builds the request via `anthropic_adapter.build_anthropic_kwargs()`. That function calls `normalize_model_name(model, preserve_dots=...)`. The `preserve_dots` argument is set by `anthropic_preserve_dots()`, which only checked for Alibaba DashScope — never for OpenCode Go. So even after Bug 1 is fixed, the API-layer call still converts `minimax-m2.7` → `minimax-m2-7`.

**Fix:**
```diff
 def anthropic_preserve_dots(self) -> bool:
-    """True when using AlibabaDashScope anthropic-compatible endpoint —
-    model names keep dots, e.g. qwen3.5-plus."""
-    if getattr(self, "provider", "") or "").lower() == "alibaba":
+    """True when using an anthropic-compatible endpoint that preserves dots in model names.
+    AlibabaDashScope keeps dots (e.g. qwen3.5-plus).
+    OpenCode Go keeps dots (e.g. minimax-m2.7). Without this, dots become hyphens → 401."""
+    if getattr(self, "provider", "") or "").lower() in {"alibaba", "opencode-go"}:
         return True
     base = (getattr(self, "base_url", "") or "").lower()
-    return "dashscope" in base or "aliyuncs" in base
+    return "dashscope" in base or "aliyuncs" in base or "opencode.ai/zen/go" in base
```

---

## Evidence

**Request dump from a failing session** (`.hermes/sessions/request_dump.json`):
```json
{
  "method": "POST",
  "url": "https://opencode.ai/zen/go/chat/completions",
  "body": { "model": "minimax-m2-7" }  // dots already became hyphens here
}
```

**Working curl with correct model name:**
```bash
curl https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/messages \
  -H "x-api-key: sk-..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "minimax-m2.7", "max_tokens": 50, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello briefly"}]}'
# Returns a valid response
```

**`config.yaml` is always correct** — Hermes stores the name properly. The mangling happens after config is loaded, during the API request build step:
```yaml
model_default: minimax-m2.7   # correct
provider: opencode-go
base_url: https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1
```

items.title: [Bug]: Provider-side HTTP 402 can kill entire gateway service instead of failing only the request
items.body:
## Bug Description
A provider-side billing/quota failure (HTTP 402 / `daily_limit_busy` / exhausted balance) can kill the entire Hermes gateway service instead of only failing the single user request.

In this environment, Hermes was running as a user systemd service for Telegram:
- service: `hermes-gateway.service`
- command: `python -m hermes_cli.main gateway run --replace`
- platform: Telegram long polling

When the upstream model provider returned HTTP 402, the whole gateway stopped polling Telegram and the bot no longer replied until the service was manually restarted.

This appears to violate the intended behavior already present in the code:
- `run_agent.py` treats non-retryable client errors as per-request failures and returns a failed result object
- `gateway/run.py` has logic to convert failed agent runs into a user-visible error response

So the expected behavior is: fail one request, keep the gateway alive.

## Expected Behavior
When a provider returns HTTP 402 (out of money / quota exhausted / `daily_limit_busy`):
- the current request should fail gracefully
- Hermes may retry/fallback if configured
- Hermes may send a friendly error back to Telegram
- **the gateway process should remain alive and continue polling**

## Actual Behavior
After the provider returned HTTP 402, the systemd gateway service stopped and Telegram replies ceased entirely until manual restart.

Observed state after the failure:
- `hermes gateway status` reported the user gateway service as stopped
- Telegram bot stopped replying
- manual `hermes gateway start` restored service

## Relevant Logs / Evidence
Service journal at the time of failure:

```text
Apr 05 10:50:41 ... APIStatusError [HTTP 402]
Apr 05 10:50:41 ... Provider: custom  Model: claude-opus-4-6
Apr 05 10:50:41 ... Endpoint: https://yunyi.cfd/claude
Apr 05 10:50:41 ... Error: HTTP 402: Insufficient available balance for new requests. Daily quota: $200.00, spent: $199.8100, in use by pending requests: $0.1900 (available: $0.0000). Please wait for ongoing requests to complete.
Apr 05 10:50:41 ... Non-retryable error (HTTP 402) — trying fallback...
Apr 05 10:50:41 ... Non-retryable client error (HTTP 402). Aborting.
Apr 05 10:50:45 systemd[721]: Stopping hermes-gateway.service - Hermes Agent Gateway - Messaging Platform Integration...
Apr 05 10:50:45 systemd[721]: Stopped hermes-gateway.service - Hermes Agent Gateway - Messaging Platform Integration.
```

The generated service unit in this environment is:

```ini
[Service]
Type=simple
ExecStart=/root/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv/bin/python -m hermes_cli.main gateway run --replace
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=30
KillMode=mixed
TimeoutStopSec=60
```

The gateway status after the incident showed:

```text
Active: inactive (dead)
Recent gateway health:
  Last shutdown reason: telegram: Telegram startup failed: Bad Gateway
```

## Why this seems like a bug
From local inspection of the installed source:

1. `run_agent.py` handles non-retryable client errors by returning a structured failure object rather than intentionally exiting the process.
2. `gateway/run.py` contains logic to surface `agent_result.get("failed")` as a user-visible error response.
3. Therefore a provider-side 402 should be contained to the request boundary.

But in practice the gateway service dies, which suggests one of:
- an exception is escaping above the intended request-failure boundary
- the gateway main loop exits when a request returns a certain failure shape
- process/cgroup isolation between gateway and agent-spawned child processes is insufficient, so failure/restart of one request destabilizes the whole service

## Environment
- Hermes installed from `NousResearch/hermes-agent`
- Observed on: 2026-04-05
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04 (server)
- Python: 3.11.15
- Gateway: Telegram (polling mode)
- Running as: user systemd service (`hermes-gateway.service`)
- Model provider involved in the failure: custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint

## Notes
This issue is **not** about Telegram credentials. Telegram config/chat registration remained valid. Restarting the gateway restored Telegram functionality immediately.

This also seems distinct from earlier Telegram transport/startup issues (for example the fallback transport / InvalidURL problem), because here the trigger was a provider-side billing/quota failure during normal request handling.

items.title: Resume interrupted gateway sessions after graceful restart
items.body:
## Summary

Graceful gateway shutdown currently interrupts in-flight sessions, but the next restart does not record or resume that interrupted work. The persisted session transcript remains, but the gateway loses the fact that a turn was actively running, any queued follow-up event waiting behind it, and the need to nudge the agent to continue.

## Proposal

- persist a small restart ledger for in-flight gateway turns during graceful shutdown
- restore those entries on the next startup and enqueue a hidden continuation turn from persisted session context
- preserve queued follow-up user input when present instead of discarding it
- make the behavior opt-in through gateway config

## Notes

- this should resume by scheduling a new hidden turn, not by trying to continue mid-tool or mid-call-stack
- approval state can be noted in the resume message, but should not be auto-approved or replayed as privileged state

items.body:
## Bug Description When a cron job delivers its response to a Matrix room, the message is sent as **plain text only** — no `formatted_body` is included in the Matrix event. This means markdown formatting produced by the agent (headers, bold, lists, code blocks, etc.) is displayed as raw syntax (`##`, `**`, `` ` ``, etc.) instead of being rendered. This affects **all** cron deliveries to Matrix, including the built-in morning briefing and any user-defined cron jobs. The normal chat path (interactive messages via the gateway) renders markdown correctly because `gateway/platforms/matrix.py` converts markdown to HTML and sets `formatted_body`. But the cron delivery path bypasses this entirely. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Configure Hermes with Matrix as a gateway platform 2. Create a cron job that delivers to Matrix: ``` /cron create --schedule "0 9 * * *" --deliver matrix --prompt "Give me a summary with ## headers and **bold** text" ``` 3. Trigger the cron job (or wait for it to fire): ``` /cron run ``` 4. Observe the delivered message in the Matrix room ## Expected Behavior The delivered message should include both: - `body`: plain text fallback (as it does now) - `format`: `"org.matrix.custom.html"` - `formatted_body`: HTML-rendered version of the markdown content For example, `## Summary` should render as a heading (or at minimum bold text), and `**important**` should render as bold. ## Actual Behavior The Matrix event contains only: ```json { "msgtype": "m.text", "body": "Cronjob Response: morning-briefing\n-------------\n\n## Good Morning!\n\nHere's your **daily briefing**...\n\nNote: The agent cannot see this message, and therefore cannot respond to it." } ``` No `formatted_body` or `format` field is present. Matrix clients display the raw markdown symbols literally. ## Affected Component - Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp) - Tools (terminal, file ops, web, code execution, etc.) ## Messaging Platform - Matrix (via the `send_message_tool.py` REST API path, not the `matrix-nio` encrypted path) ## Operating System Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie) — Docker container ## Python Version 3.13.5 ## Hermes Version 0.7.0 ## Relevant Logs / Traceback No errors — the message sends successfully, it's just missing the HTML formatting. The Matrix API happily accepts a plain-text-only payload. ## Root Cause Analysis The issue spans two files: ### 1. `tools/send_message_tool.py` — `_send_matrix()` (line ~721) This function builds a hardcoded plain-text payload with no markdown-to-HTML conversion: ```python async def _send_matrix(token, extra, chat_id, message): # ... async with session.put( url, headers=headers, json={"msgtype": "m.text", "body": message} ) as resp: # ... ``` There is no attempt to convert markdown to HTML or include `formatted_body`. ### 2. `cron/scheduler.py` — `_deliver_result()` (line ~133) This function calls `_send_to_platform()` (which calls `_send_matrix()`) and passes the raw text content. It has no platform-specific formatting logic: ```python coro = _send_to_platform( platform, pconfig, chat_id, delivery_content, thread_id=thread_id ) ``` ### Contrast with the working chat path The interactive Matrix adapter in `gateway/platforms/matrix.py` has a `_markdown_to_html()` method that: 1. Converts markdown to HTML using the `markdown` Python library 2. Sets `formatted_body` and `format: "org.matrix.custom.html"` on the event The cron delivery path completely bypasses this adapter and goes directly through `send_message_tool.py`'s minimal REST implementation. ## Proposed Fix Update `_send_matrix()` in `tools/send_message_tool.py` to optionally convert markdown to HTML: ```python async def _send_matrix(token, extra, chat_id, message): # ... existing setup code ... msg_content = {"msgtype": "m.text", "body": message} # Convert markdown to HTML for formatted_body try: import markdown as md html = md.markdown( message, extensions=["nl2br", "fenced_code", "tables"] ) if html != message: msg_content["format"] = "org.matrix.custom.html" msg_content["formatted_body"] = html except ImportError: pass # graceful fallback to plain text async with session.put(url, headers=headers, json=msg_content) as resp: # ... existing response handling ... ``` This is a minimal, backward-compatible change — if the `markdown` library isn't installed, it silently falls back to plain text (current behavior). The `markdown` library is already a dependency used by `gateway/platforms/matrix.py`. ### Additional note on Element X (Android) Element X does not render standard HTML header tags (`

`–`

items.title: bug(gateway): commands (/new, /undo, etc.) are ignored while agent is running a tool
