labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Bug Description

When the agent is executing a tool (especially long-running ones like `terminal`), all gateway commands — `/new`, `/undo`, `/stop`, etc. — are ignored or queued without being processed. The agent continues running until the tool naturally completes.

- `/stop` is partially handled: it sets `_interrupt_requested` and force-removes from `_running_agents`, but cannot cancel the in-flight tool execution itself (addressed in #5243).
- `/new` and all other commands are completely blocked — the gateway appears to queue or discard them while the session is locked.

## Expected Behavior

All gateway commands should be processed immediately, regardless of whether an agent is currently running:

- `/new` → force-stop current agent, start new session
- `/undo` → interrupt current operation, undo last message
- `/stop` → interrupt and stop (partially working)

## Root Cause

In `gateway/run.py`, `_handle_message()` checks if the session is in `_running_agents` (line ~1763). If the agent is running, incoming messages (including commands) are either queued or silently dropped. Only `/stop` has special-case handling to force-unlock the session.

## Proposed Fix

1. **Command pre-processing**: Before checking `_running_agents`, parse the incoming message for known commands (`/new`, `/undo`, `/stop`, `/yolo`, `/compact`, etc.)
2. **Stateful commands take priority**: If the message is a command, process it immediately — call `agent.interrupt()`, force-remove from `_running_agents`, then execute the command's logic.
3. **Non-command messages**: Continue current behavior (queue for the running agent).

This is similar to how signal handlers work in Unix — SIGINT (Ctrl+C) interrupts a blocking syscall, regardless of what the process is doing.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.7.0 (2026.4.3)
- Python 3.11
- Platform: Telegram gateway (also affects CLI)

## Related

- #5243 — fixes `terminal_tool` not responding to interrupts during execution

When Hermes calls MCP server tools, all parameters arrive as JSON strings regardless of their declared type. Object parameters arrive as stringified JSON, and numeric parameters arrive as string representations of numbers.

items.title: bug: gateway _run_agent shadows message and breaks Codex path
items.body:
## Description

`GatewayRunner._run_agent()` defines an inner `run_sync()` closure that later reassigns `message` when prepending a pending model-switch note. That makes Python treat `message` as a local variable for the whole closure, so earlier reads fail with `UnboundLocalError` before the agent even starts.

## Impact

This breaks gateway execution paths that reach the closure before any pending note handling, including the Codex refresh test path.

## Root Cause

Inside `gateway/run.py`, `run_sync()` does:

```python
if _msn:
    message = _msn + "\n\n" + message
```

But `message` is also read earlier in the same closure:

```python
turn_route = self._resolve_turn_agent_config(message, model, runtime_kwargs)
```

That local assignment shadows the outer `_run_agent(..., message=...)` parameter.

## Proposed Fix

Stop rebinding `message` inside the closure. Use a separate local like `prompt_message` for the final `run_conversation(...)` call.

## Regression Test

`tests/test_codex_execution_paths.py::test_gateway_run_agent_codex_path_handles_internal_401_refresh`

## Environment

Observed on current `upstream/main` as of 2026-04-05.

## Summary

MemoryProvider prefetch/recall can be injected in a way the model treats as shared discourse.

The injected block is not visible in the transcript or session log, but the assistant can still respond to it as if the user saw it.

## Why this matters

- likely affects all memory providers using the MemoryProvider prefetch path, not just Honcho
- provider/model differences probably only change how obvious the leak is
- this is a core framing problem, not a provider-specific retrieval problem

- hidden recall is being framed too close to the user-message / discourse layer
- core should keep provider prefetch in ephemeral system-only context, never the user-visible/shared-conversation lane

- inject recognizable hidden provider context
- ask an unrelated user question
- assert final response does not quote, paraphrase, or otherwise treat the hidden block as shared visible context

- is the leak happening only through the MemoryProvider `prefetch()` path, or are there other hidden-context injection paths with the same framing problem?
- should all provider recall be routed through ephemeral system context by default, with explicit opt-in if a provider wants user-message injection?
- do plugin `pre_llm_call` injections with `target="user_message"` need stronger separation from private/internal context?
- should we add a final-response guard that blocks obvious internal context headers from surfacing unless the user explicitly asks for internals?

What happens:

When the gateway agent delegates a task via delegate_task, the child agent occasionally loses all terminal and file tools, leaving it with only process (which has no check_fn). The subagent becomes unable to execute commands or manipulate files.

2 - Log check_fn failures at WARNING level regardless of quiet flag, so silent tool loss is diagnosable.

Subagent terminal calls should succeed.

As stated before, no error output as `registry.get_definitions()` silently swallows check_fn failures when quiet=True which is always the case for subagents.

Tools (terminal, file ops, web, code execution, etc.)

N/A (CLI only)

macOS Tahoe 26.4 (Darwin arm64, Apple Silicon)

No logs

`check_terminal_requirements()` (tools/terminal_tool.py:1347) runs `subprocess.run([docker, "version"], timeout=5)` (line 1364) on `every get_tool_definitions()` call with no result caching. ## Bug Description

The terminal output redaction system (which scrubs secrets like API keys from display output) is writing `***` directly into source files on disk, rather than only filtering display output.

## Affected File

`plugins/memory/honcho/client.py` line 312 was corrupted from:
```python
api_key=api_key,
```
to:
```python
api_key=***
```

This caused a `SyntaxError` every time the module was imported, which was silently caught by `is_available()`'s bare `except Exception: return False`, making Honcho permanently report as 'not available' with no visible error.

## Impact

- `hermes memory status` always shows `Status: not available ✗` even with valid credentials and a reachable Honcho instance
- Honcho memory is silently disabled for all sessions — no warnings, no errors surfaced to the user
- The root cause is invisible without reading the source file directly

1. Run `hermes` in an environment where `HONCHO_API_KEY` is set
2. Check `plugins/memory/honcho/client.py` line 312 on disk
3. Observe `api_key=***` instead of `api_key=api_key,`

## Fix Applied

Manually patched line 312 back to `api_key=api_key,`. `hermes memory status` immediately returned `available ✓`.

## Root Cause

The PII/secrets redaction system must be writing filtered output back to the source file rather than only filtering the display stream. Redaction should be strictly read-only — it should never write to disk.

## Severity

**Critical** — silently disables a core feature (memory) with no user-visible error, and corrupts installed source files.

items.title: MCP OAuth: port collision on concurrent auth + redirect URI mismatch on restart
items.body:
## Bug Description

Two related bugs in `tools/mcp_oauth.py` cause MCP OAuth to fail reliably when multiple OAuth-backed MCP servers are configured:

### 1. Port collision on concurrent OAuth flows (Address already in use)

`build_oauth_auth()` stores the callback port in a **module-level global** `_oauth_port`. When multiple MCP servers need OAuth simultaneously (common on startup), each call to `build_oauth_auth()` overwrites the global with a new port. All concurrent `_wait_for_callback()` calls then try to bind the **same** port, causing `OSError: [Errno 48] Address already in use` for all but the first.

This was partially addressed in #2552 but the fix used a shared global which doesn't solve the concurrent case.

### 2. Redirect URI mismatch after restart (invalid_grant)

Each restart picks a **new random port** via `_find_free_port()`, but the OAuth client is already registered with the provider (e.g. Notion) using the **old** port's redirect URI. The provider rejects the token exchange with:

```
Token exchange failed (400): {"error":"invalid_grant","error_description":"Invalid redirect URI"}
```

Deleting the client registration file forces re-registration but shouldn't be necessary.

## Reproduction

1. Configure 2+ OAuth MCP servers (e.g. Notion, Todoist, Clay)
2. Delete cached tokens to force re-auth
3. Start Hermes — observe "Address already in use" errors for all but one server
4. Even if only one server needs auth, restart Hermes — observe "Invalid redirect URI" error

## Fix

1. Replace the shared `_oauth_port` global with per-server ports via closure (`_make_wait_for_callback(port)`)
2. On startup, check for an existing client registration and reuse its redirect URI port before falling back to a new random port

items.title: [Bug]: Gateway and CLI ignore model.provider config — fall back to OpenRouter when OPENROUTER_API_KEY exists

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Problem

When running Hermes via the gateway (Discord/Telegram) **or CLI**, the agent ignores the explicitly configured `model.provider` and `model.base_url` in `config.yaml` and routes all requests through OpenRouter if `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` is present in the environment.

This causes unexpected billing on OpenRouter even when the user has configured a different provider (e.g., MiniMax, Ollama Cloud, Anthropic) and never intended to use OpenRouter.

## Root Cause

In `gateway/run.py`, `_resolve_runtime_agent_kwargs()` calls:

```python
runtime = resolve_runtime_provider(
    requested=os.getenv("HERMES_INFERENCE_PROVIDER"),
)
```

This passes **only** the env var — not the config's `model.provider`. When `HERMES_INFERENCE_PROVIDER` is unset, `resolve_runtime_provider()` defaults to `"auto"`, which eventually falls through to `_resolve_openrouter_runtime()` at `runtime_provider.py:727-733`.

The `_resolve_openrouter_runtime()` function only respects `model.base_url` when `model.provider` is `"auto"` or `"custom"`:

```python
if requested_norm == "auto":
    if not cfg_provider or cfg_provider == "auto":
        use_config_base_url = True
```

If the user has configured `model.provider: minimax` (or any specific provider), the config base_url is ignored and OpenRouter is used instead.

The CLI has the same bug at `cli.py:1220-2077` — it checks `CLI_CONFIG["model"].get("provider")` but still passes `requested="auto"` to `resolve_runtime_provider()` when no env var is set, triggering the same fallback path.

## Reproduction

1. Configure Hermes with a non-OpenRouter provider:

```yaml
model:
  base_url: https://api.minimax.io/anthropic
  default: MiniMax-M2.7
  provider: minimax
```

2. Ensure `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` is set in `~/.hermes/.env` (from a previous config or fresh key)
3. Start the gateway: `hermes gateway` (or use CLI: `hermes chat`)
4. Send a message via Discord/Telegram (or chat in CLI)
5. **Expected:** Requests go to `api.minimax.io` using MiniMax-M2.7
6. **Actual:** Requests go to `openrouter.ai` — model may be auto-selected (e.g., GLM-5), and OpenRouter credits are consumed

## Impact

- **Severity:** High — users unknowingly billed for API calls when they configured a different provider
- **Affected users:** Anyone using the gateway or CLI with a non-OpenRouter provider who also has `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` in their environment
- **Financial impact:** Direct — unexpected API charges on OpenRouter

## Related Issues

- #4172 — Similar bug reported for CLI/setup wizard, claimed fixed by #4165, but the fix only works for `provider: auto` or `provider: custom`. Specific providers (minimax, anthropic, etc.) still fall through to OpenRouter.
- #3535 — Config.yaml model key silently ignored

## Proposed Fix

`gateway/run.py:_resolve_runtime_agent_kwargs()` and CLI initialization should read `model.provider` and `model.base_url` from config and pass them as explicit overrides to `resolve_runtime_provider()`:

```python
def _resolve_runtime_agent_kwargs() -> dict:
    from hermes_cli.runtime_provider import resolve_runtime_provider, format_runtime_provider_error
    from hermes_cli.config import load_config
    
    config = load_config()
    model_cfg = config.get("model", {})
    
    # Use config provider/base_url if HERMES_INFERENCE_PROVIDER not set
    env_provider = os.getenv("HERMES_INFERENCE_PROVIDER")
    if env_provider:
        requested = env_provider
        explicit_base_url = None
    else:
        requested = model_cfg.get("provider", "auto")
        explicit_base_url = model_cfg.get("base_url")
    
    try:
        runtime = resolve_runtime_provider(
            requested=requested,
            explicit_base_url=explicit_base_url,
        )
    except Exception as exc:
        raise RuntimeError(format_runtime_provider_error(exc)) from exc
    
    return {
        "api_key": runtime.get("api_key"),
        "base_url": runtime.get("base_url"),
        "provider": runtime.get("provider"),
        "api_mode": runtime.get("api_mode"),
        "command": runtime.get("command"),
        "args": list(runtime.get("args") or []),
        "credential_pool": runtime.get("credential_pool"),
    }
```

This ensures the gateway respects `model.provider` config before falling back to auto-detection.

items.body:
## Bug: /btw command fails with validation error when session has transcript history

### Description
The `/btw` (by the way) command fails with a cryptic API validation error when there's an existing session transcript. The error message indicates that `session_meta` entries are being passed to the LLM API, which rejects them as invalid.

### Error Message
```
API call failed after 3 retries: HTTP 400: Error code: 400 - {'error': "[object Object] failed the following checks:
[object Object] failed the following checks:
...
null failed the following checks:
null is not a string
null is not an array
session_meta is not equa
```

### Root Cause
In `gateway/run.py`, the `_run_btw_task()` method loads the session transcript to provide context for the side question:

```python
history_snapshot = self.session_store.load_transcript(session_entry.session_id)
```

However, `load_transcript()` returns the raw transcript including `session_meta` entries (internal metadata with tool definitions, model info, etc.). These entries have `"role": "session_meta"` which is **not a valid role** for the LLM API.

The main message handler at line 5798 correctly filters out `session_meta` entries:
```python
if role in ("session_meta",):
    continue
```

But the `/btw` handler was missing this filtering.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Start a conversation (any platform)
2. Have some back-and-forth to populate the session transcript
3. Run `/btw <any question>`
4. The command fails with the validation error

### Expected Behavior
The `/btw` command should filter out `session_meta` entries from the conversation history before passing to the AI agent, just like the main message handler does.

### Proposed Fix
Filter `session_meta` entries from the loaded transcript:

```python
raw_history = self.session_store.load_transcript(session_entry.session_id)
# Filter out session_meta entries (internal bookkeeping, not for LLM API)
history_snapshot = [
    msg for msg in raw_history
    if msg.get("role") != "session_meta"
]
```

### Additional Context
- CLI mode `/btw` is not affected because `self.conversation_history` in the CLI doesn't include `session_meta` entries
- This only affects the gateway mode where transcripts are stored with metadata
- The fix aligns with how the main handler processes history (line 5798)

items.body:
## Bug

Every incoming Telegram message crashes with `UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'message'` in `gateway/run.py` inside `run_sync()`.

## Root Cause

Python variable scoping issue. In `run_sync()` (nested inside `_run_agent()`), line ~6544 conditionally assigns to `message`:

```python
if _msn:
    message = _msn + "\n\n" + message
```

Because Python sees `message =` anywhere in the function body, it classifies `message` as a **local** variable for the entire `run_sync()` scope. When `_msn` is `None` (the common case — no pending model switch), the assignment never executes, but `message` is already classified as local. Line ~6330 then hits:

```python
turn_route = self._resolve_turn_agent_config(message, model, runtime_kwargs)
```

→ `UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'message' where it is not associated with a value`

The `message` parameter belongs to the enclosing `_run_agent()`, but the conditional assignment in `run_sync()` shadows it.

## Traceback

```
ERROR gateway.run: Agent error in session agent:main:telegram:dm:1326780748
  File "gateway/run.py", line 2733, in _handle_message_with_agent
    agent_result = await self._run_agent(...)
  File "gateway/run.py", line 6676, in _run_agent
    response = await asyncio.wait_for(...)
  File "gateway/run.py", line 6243, in run_sync
    turn_route = self._resolve_turn_agent_config(message, model, runtime_kwargs)
UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'message' where it is not associated with a value
```

## Fix

Use a new local variable instead of reassigning `message`:

```python
# Before (broken):
if _msn:
    message = _msn + "\n\n" + message

result = agent.run_conversation(message, ...)

# After (fixed):
final_message = (_msn + "\n\n" + message) if _msn else message

result = agent.run_conversation(final_message, ...)
```

## Version

`v2026.4.3-77-g70f79804` — bug also present on `origin/main` at the same lines.

## Impact

**Every** Telegram (and likely Discord/Slack) message fails. The gateway connects fine, receives messages, but crashes on every response attempt. The `_pending_model_notes` feature (from `/model` switch) introduced this regression.

items.title: [Bug] Dynamic memory provider tools (honcho_profile, honcho_search, honcho_context, honcho_conclude) fail with 'Unknown tool' in sequential dispatch path
items.body:
## Summary

When `memory.provider=honcho` is configured, the four Honcho memory tools (`honcho_profile`, `honcho_search`, `honcho_context`, `honcho_conclude`) are registered in the agent's tool surface and visible to the model, but calling them returns `"Unknown tool"`.

This is because `_execute_tool_calls_sequential()` in `run_agent.py` is missing the memory provider dispatch that already exists in `_invoke_tool()`.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent (self-hosted, latest)
- `memory.provider=honcho` with self-hosted Honcho instance
- Reproducible on both CLI and Gateway (Telegram) modes
- `recallMode=hybrid`

## Observed Behavior

1. Honcho backend is healthy — API responds, messages are stored, deriver processes observations
2. Auto-injection works — `## Honcho Context` blocks appear in system prompts with populated representations
3. Tool schemas ARE injected into `self.tools` — the model sees and attempts to call `honcho_profile`, `honcho_search`, etc.
4. But all four tool calls fail with `"Unknown tool"`

## Root Cause

There are **two tool dispatch paths** in `run_agent.py`, and only one handles memory provider tools:

### Concurrent path (WORKS) — `_invoke_tool()` (~line 5620)
```python
elif self._memory_manager and self._memory_manager.has_tool(function_name):
    return self._memory_manager.handle_tool_call(function_name, function_args)
```

### Sequential path (BUGGY) — `_execute_tool_calls_sequential()` (~line 5847)
The sequential path has an if/elif chain for agent-level tools (`todo`, `session_search`, `memory`, `clarify`, `delegate_task`), then falls through to `handle_function_call()` → `registry.dispatch()`. 

Honcho tools are **not in the registry** — they were removed at `model_tools.py` line 159 when they became a memory provider plugin:
```python
# "tools.honcho_tools",  # Removed — Honcho is now a memory provider plugin
```

So the sequential fallthrough hits `registry.dispatch()` which has no handler for honcho tools.

## Why Auto-Injection Works But Direct Calls Don't

- **Prefetch/system prompt injection** goes through `MemoryManager` directly (`_memory_manager.prefetch_all()`, `_memory_manager.build_system_prompt()`) — no dispatch involved
- **Tool surface registration** works correctly — `AIAgent.__init__()` appends memory provider schemas to `self.tools` and `self.valid_tool_names` (lines ~1092-1099)
- **But sequential dispatch** never routes honcho tool calls to `_memory_manager`

## Suggested Fix

Add the memory provider check to the sequential path's if/elif chain in `_execute_tool_calls_sequential()`, between the `delegate_task` handler and the final `handle_function_call()` fallthrough:

```python
# After delegate_task handler, before handle_function_call fallthrough
elif self._memory_manager and self._memory_manager.has_tool(function_name):
    result = self._memory_manager.handle_tool_call(function_name, function_args)
```

This mirrors the existing check in `_invoke_tool()` at line ~5620.

## Key Files

| File | Relevance |
|------|-----------|
| `run_agent.py` ~line 5620 | `_invoke_tool()` — has correct memory manager dispatch |
| `run_agent.py` ~line 5847-6012 | `_execute_tool_calls_sequential()` — missing memory manager dispatch |
| `run_agent.py` ~line 1092-1099 | `AIAgent.__init__()` — tool surface assembly (correct) |
| `model_tools.py` line 159 | Honcho removed from registry |
| `agent/memory_manager.py` lines 207-229 | `has_tool()` and `handle_tool_call()` |
| `plugins/memory/honcho/__init__.py` lines 33-112, 606-672 | Tool schemas and handlers |

items.title: [Bug]: HERMES_FENCE markers leak into file content via ShellFileOperations — corrupts source files silently

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Bug Description

`ShellFileOperations.read_file()` reads files by shelling out to `sed` via the terminal execution layer, which wraps every command with `printf HERMES_FENCE; cmd; printf HERMES_FENCE` markers. The `_extract_fenced_output()` function is supposed to strip these markers, but intermittently fails — causing `__HERMES_FENCE_a9f7b3__` text and associated BEL chars (`\x07`) / OSC escape sequences (`\x1b]0;...`) to leak into the file content returned to the model.

When the model subsequently uses `write_file` or `patch` with this contaminated content, the fence markers get baked into the actual source files on disk.

## Impact

- **Silent file corruption** — files compile/run fine until the garbage lands on a critical line
- **Cascading failures** — corrupted gateway files (`gateway/run.py`, `gateway/platforms/base.py`) crashed the Telegram gateway service, which hit systemd restart limits and stayed dead for 24+ hours
- **Cross-project contamination** — corruption found in files across unrelated projects edited in the same session
- **Not caught by ANSI stripping** — commit `934fbe3c` strips ANSI escape sequences at the source, but `__HERMES_FENCE_a9f7b3__` is plain ASCII text, not an ANSI sequence, so it passes through the strip_ansi() filter

## Root Cause

`tools/file_operations.py` line ~530:

```python
# ShellFileOperations.read_file()
read_cmd = f"sed -n '{{offset}},{end_line}p' {self._escape_shell_arg(path)}"
read_result = self._exec(read_cmd)
```

`self._exec()` goes through `LocalEnvironment.execute()` which wraps the command:

```
printf __HERMES_FENCE_a9f7b3__; sed -n 1,500p /path/to/file; __hermes_rc=$?; printf __HERMES_FENCE_a9f7b3__
```

Then `_extract_fenced_output()` (`tools/environments/local.py` line ~293) tries to extract content between fences. When this extraction fails or partially succeeds, the raw fence markers end up in the tool result returned to the model.

## Reproduction

This is intermittent but frequent enough to hit multiple times per week in normal usage. The corruption pattern is always the same — line 1 (or the last line) of the file gets prefixed/suffixed with:

```
'\\x07__HERMES_FENCE_a9f7b3__\\x1b]0;cat '/path/to/file' 2> /dev/null\\x07
```

## Existing Mitigations (Insufficient)

| Commit | What it does | Why it's not enough |
|--------|-------------|----------------------|
| `934fbe3c` | Strip ANSI at terminal output source | Fence markers are plain ASCII, not ANSI |
| `fa6f0695` | Strip ANSI from write_file/patch content | Same — doesn't catch fence text |
| `f803f663` | Fix heredoc EOF merging with fence wrapper | Only fixes one specific failure mode |
| `11615014` | Introduced fence markers + extraction | The extraction itself is the failure point |

## Proposed Fix

**For the local backend**: `ShellFileOperations` should use Python's native `open()` / `pathlib.Path.read_text()` for file I/O instead of shelling out to `sed`, `cat`, `head`, `wc`. This completely bypasses the terminal execution layer and its fence marker wrapping. Shell-based file ops should only be used for remote backends (SSH, Docker) where native Python I/O isn't available.

**Alternative (less invasive)**: Add a post-extraction sanitizer in `_extract_fenced_output()` or in `ShellFileOperations.read_file()` that explicitly strips `__HERMES_FENCE_*` markers and BEL/OSC sequences from the returned content:

```python
import re
def _sanitize_fence_leaks(text: str) -> str:
    """Strip any leaked fence markers and associated terminal garbage."""
    text = re.sub(r"'?\\x07?__HERMES_FENCE_[a-f0-9]+__", "", text)
    text = re.sub(r"\\x1b\][^\\x07]*\\x07", "", text)
    text = text.replace("\\x07", "")
    return text.strip("'\\n") + "\\n" if text.strip() else text
```

## Environment

- **OS:** Ubuntu 24.04
- **Hermes Agent:** Latest main (commit `2556cfda`)
- **Backend:** Local (native Ubuntu, not Docker/SSH)
- **Affected files:** `.py`, `.tsx`, `.ts`, `.json` — any file type
- **Gateway:** systemd user service (`hermes-gateway.service`)

## Related Issues

- #4451 — patch tool `await` corruption (different root cause: redaction regex)
- #3587 — heredoc fence leak (closed, partially addressed by `f803f663`)
- #3801 — patch-tool redaction corruption restoring terminalbench2_env.py

items.body:
## Summary

Self-hosted Honcho memory silently fails to initialize when using `ghcr.io/plastic-labs/honcho:latest` (currently v3.0.5), because the `honcho-ai` SDK bundled in the Hermes image is 2.1.0, which is incompatible with the v3 API.

## What happens

Hermes logs on every startup:
```
WARNING plugins.memory.honcho: Honcho init failed: An unexpected error occurred
```

No memory is saved or retrieved across sessions.

## Root cause

The Honcho server v3.x exposes a `/v3/` API with a different resource shape. The `honcho-ai` 2.1.0 SDK calls a v2-era API — specifically, `h.workspaces` is a bound method in 2.x, not a resource object, so `h.workspaces.get_or_create()` raises:

```
AttributeError: 'function' object has no attribute 'get_or_create'
```

Confirmed by running inside the hermes container:
```python
from honcho import Honcho
h = Honcho(base_url='http://honcho-api:8000')
h.workspaces.get_or_create(name='hermes')
# AttributeError: 'function' object has no attribute 'get_or_create'
```

## Versions

- `nousresearch/hermes-agent:latest` — `honcho-ai` 2.1.0
- `ghcr.io/plastic-labs/honcho:latest` — Honcho server 3.0.5
- `pyproject.toml` in this repo: `honcho = ["honcho-ai>=2.0.1,<3"]`

## Attempted workaround

Pinning Honcho server to `v2.5.1` resolves the SDK mismatch but introduces a separate incompatibility: v2.5.1 rejects `EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=openrouter` (only `openai`/`gemini` accepted), which the latest Hermes `honcho.env.secret` template uses.

## Expected fix

Update the `honcho-ai` dependency in Hermes to `>=3.0.0` and update the Honcho plugin code to match the v3 SDK API. The Honcho server `latest` tag should be the target.

items.title: Provider cooldown / circuit breaker for persistent failures

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Problem

When a provider returns 401/403 or persistent rate limits, Hermes retries `max_retries` times, possibly tries fallback, but on the **next iteration loop pass** it hits the same broken provider again. No memory of prior failures carries across iterations within a session.

This means a rate-limited provider gets hammered on every single tool-call iteration until the session ends or the user intervenes.

## Proposed Solution

Add a lightweight process-scoped `ProviderCooldownTracker` that:
- Records failure reasons per `(provider, base_url)` key
- Implements escalating cooldown: 30s → 60s → 5min for transient errors, 5min → 10min → 30min for permanent errors
- Is checked before each API call in `run_conversation()`
- On cooldown: triggers fallback activation immediately
- Resets on successful calls (circuit breaker close)

Thread-safe singleton — works across concurrent gateway sessions.

## Benefits

- Stops hammering broken providers across iterations
- Graceful degradation with automatic recovery
- Pairs naturally with the existing fallback chain

items.title: Feature: Cron job output chaining — let one job's output feed into another
items.body:
## Problem

There is currently no mechanism for one cron job's output to be available to another cron job. Each job runs in a completely isolated session (`cron/scheduler.py` creates a fresh `AIAgent` per run with its own session ID). If job A discovers something and job B needs to act on it, users must wire the data through files on disk manually (e.g. job A writes to a file, job B's prompt references that file).

## Current behavior

- Each cron job gets an isolated agent session (`cron_{job_id}_{timestamp}`)
- Job output is delivered to the configured target (Telegram, Discord, etc.) and saved to the session DB
- No job can reference another job's output or declare a dependency on another job
- The `script` field lets a Python script run before the agent and inject stdout into the prompt, which is the closest workaround — but requires the user to write a script that reads from wherever the previous job saved its output

## Desired behavior

A first-class way to chain cron jobs so one job's output can feed into the next. Possible approaches:

### Option A: Explicit chaining via job dependencies
Add a `depends_on` or `after` field to the job schema that references another job ID. When job B depends on job A:
- Job B waits for job A to complete before running
- Job A's final output is injected into job B's prompt (similar to how `script` stdout is injected)

### Option B: Named output slots
Jobs can write to named output keys (e.g. `output_key: "daily_findings"`). Other jobs reference these via `input_from: "daily_findings"`, which injects the most recent output from that key into the prompt.

### Option C: Shared context file (lightweight)
Provide a convention/helper for jobs to share state through a well-known location (`~/.hermes/cron/shared/`), with the cronjob tool exposing a `context` parameter that auto-reads from a named file before execution. Less magical than A/B but trivial to implement.

## Use case

> *"One [cron job] finds something, but the other can't see what it found unless I wire it through files manually."*
> — @witcheer

## Files involved

- `cron/jobs.py` — job schema, CronJob dataclass
- `cron/scheduler.py` — job execution, prompt building (`_build_job_prompt`)
- `tools/cronjob_tool.py` — cronjob tool schema (would need new fields)
- `hermes_state.py` — SessionDB (could query previous job outputs)

items.title: Preserve partial stream content on retry instead of restarting from scratch

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Problem

When a stream fails mid-delivery (connection drop, SSE error), Hermes discards all received content and restarts the entire request. For long responses this wastes tokens and time — the model regenerates content it already produced.

## Proposed Solution

On partial stream failure, save the accumulated text/tool-call content before retrying. If the retry succeeds, either: (a) use the new complete response, or (b) if the new response appears to be a continuation, merge the partial with the new content. The streaming path already tracks accumulated content via response objects — this is about preserving it across retry boundaries.

## Problem

Since v0.7.0 (#3934), installed skills are surfaced in Telegram's bot command picker. Discord has no equivalent — skills can only be invoked by typing \`/skill-name\` as raw text, which means they are invisible to users browsing the \`/\` autocomplete menu.

## Expected Behavior

Installed skills should appear in Discord's native slash command menu (registered via \`app_commands.Group\` or individual \`@tree.command()\` entries), matching what Telegram already does.

## Current Behavior

\`_register_slash_commands()\` in \`gateway/platforms/discord.py\` only registers hardcoded built-in commands. It never calls \`scan_skill_commands()\` or \`get_skill_commands()\` from \`agent/skill_commands.py\`. Skills are dispatched via text parsing in \`gateway/run.py\` but never registered with Discord's application command tree.

## Suggested Approach

Follow the same pattern used for Telegram in \`hermes_cli/commands.py\`:

1. Call \`scan_skill_commands()\` (already exists in \`agent/skill_commands.py\`) during \`_register_slash_commands()\`.
2. Register each skill as a subcommand under a \`/skills\` \`app_commands.Group\`, or as individual top-level commands if the count is low enough.
3. Respect the Discord guild limit of **100 slash commands** — log a warning and skip overflow entries (same cap-handling pattern as Telegram's 100-command limit in #3934).
4. Respect per-platform disabled skills (already handled in \`gateway/run.py\` dispatch, needs to be mirrored at registration time).

There is already an open PR (#2561) that takes a partial approach (registering \`quick_commands\` aliases as a \`/skills\` group) — this issue is the broader ask to include all installed skills.

## References

- v0.7.0 Telegram implementation: #3934
- Partial Discord PR (quick_commands only, not merged): #2561
- Discord slash command disable request (shows demand for control over registration): #4881

items.title: Simplification Phase 3: Move from edge-LLM to centralized Compiler
items.body:
# PLAN: Dumb Sensors, Smart Compiler (Simplification Phase 3)

## 1. Context & Pathology (What Failed)
In the previous architecture, 12 independent research sensors (Exa, Reddit, Apify, etc.) were burdened with two fundamentally opposing tasks:
1. **Mechanical I/O:** Scraping unstructured data from target endpoints.
2. **Cognitive Reasoning:** Using local LLMs to map the unstructured text into a rigid McKinsey Pydantic ontology on the fly.

**The Failure:** The system collapsed under validation errors (e.g., `pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidationError`). Sensors organically discovered real signals (like a competitor mentioned on Reddit) but hallucinated non-compliant schema tags (e.g., `node_type: 'Competitor'` instead of `Company` with a `COMPETES_WITH` edge). 
This violated Karpathy's "Bounded Autonomy" principle—the edge agents were doing too much. Merging 8 fragmented, hallucinated JSON graphs proved mathematically fragile.

## 2. The Paradigm Shift (The Goal)
We are moving to absolute separation of I/O and Compute:
- **Mechanical Layer:** Scrapers just scrape. They dump raw text/JSON with metadata into `/raw`. Zero LLMs.
- **Compiler Layer:** A single agent reads all of `/raw`, has full context, and makes exactly *one* LLM call to extract the `GraphDTO` and build the `/wiki`.
- **Observation Layer:** The compiler writes missing data gaps to `open_questions.md`, which the scrapers read on the next cycle. The file system is the database.

---

## 3. Execution Steps

### STEP 1: Destroy Edge Cognition
*   **Objective:** Strip all LLM, Instructor, and Pydantic logic from the 12 files in `sensors/` and `ingestors/`.
*   **Why:** Scraping must never fail due to a prompt hallucination or schema validation error.
*   **Success Criterion:** Sensors write plain text or flat JSON to `raw/<sensor_name>.json/md` containing ONLY the scraped evidence and source URL.

### STEP 2: Centralize the Compiler
*   **Objective:** Delete `boardroom/merger.py` (which tried to merge fragmented graphs). Create `boardroom/compiler.py` to ingest the entire `raw/` directory into a single context window.
*   **Why:** Only the compiler possesses the ontology rules. Supplying it with all data at once prevents edge-case hallucinations and allows cross-referencing.
*   **Success Criterion:** `compiler.py` makes one Instructor API call to output `market_graph.json` and perfectly formatted `/wiki/` Markdown files.

### STEP 3: Implement the Feedback Loop (Autonomy)
*   **Objective:** Modify `compiler.py` to evaluate the generated graph for blank spots (e.g., missing pricing, no known competitors) based on the ontology.
*   **Why:** Agents shouldn't chat to figure out what to do. They read `open_questions.md`, realize they need to search for "[Company] competitors", and execute.
*   **Success Criterion:** A populated `/wiki/open_questions.md` file containing explicit search string instructions for the next swarm run.

### STEP 4: Purge Testing Theater
*   **Objective:** Delete obsolete schema mappers, fragmented output validators, and legacy graph unit tests. Remove `lane_mappers.py`, `test_sensor_graph_fragments.py`, `test_agent_outputs.py`.
*   **Why:** "Clean up your own mess." Tests pointing to deprecated cognitive layers are technical debt, not safeguards.
*   **Success Criterion:** The `tests/` directory only tests the compiler's output and API connectivity.

items.title: [Feature]: official MongoDB memory provider
items.body:
## Problem or Use Case

Hermes already has a first-class memory-provider architecture, but there is no official MongoDB-backed memory provider yet.

Right now, anyone who wants to use MongoDB as an external long-term memory backend with Hermes would need to maintain a private fork or a local-only integration. That creates setup friction, makes testing and review harder, and prevents a clean official path for a broadly useful database-backed memory provider.

Important boundary: this proposal is about adding a thin official Hermes provider for a MongoDB-backed memory backend. It is not about changing Hermes’s built-in memory model or coupling Hermes core to a specific external project implementation.

## Proposed Solution

Add an official `mongodb` memory provider under the existing memory-provider architecture, using the current `MemoryProvider` interface and discovery flow.

Planned first PR scope:
- `plugins/memory/mongodb/__init__.py`
- `plugins/memory/mongodb/plugin.yaml`
- `plugins/memory/mongodb/README.md`
- focused provider tests for discovery, config, availability, prefetch, sync_turn, tool routing, and graceful failure

Design constraints for the first PR:
- the backend implementation remains separate from Hermes core
- the Hermes integration is a thin provider shim only
- built-in `MEMORY.md` / `USER.md` stays always-on and unchanged
- provider is fully optional via `memory.provider: mongodb`
- provider-specific config/env should be namespaced for the MongoDB provider itself
- target is zero core behavior changes in Hermes; if any tiny harness change is needed, it should be discussed separately before landing

Why this should be a memory provider instead of a skill:
- it needs the native memory lifecycle (`initialize`, `prefetch`, `sync_turn`, `on_memory_write`, `shutdown`)
- it needs provider-managed config/auth through `hermes memory setup`
- it may expose provider-specific memory tools through `get_tool_schemas()`
- this is exactly the integration shape the current memory-provider system was designed for

Validation plan:
- unit tests for provider loading, config resolution, availability checks, and mocked HTTP flows
- tests for non-primary-context safety and graceful degradation
- manual verification through `hermes memory setup`, provider activation, and end-to-end turn sync
- cross-platform-safe path handling through `HERMES_HOME`

Maintenance commitment:
- I plan to implement and maintain the provider
- I will keep MongoDB-provider-specific logic out of Hermes core as much as possible
- I will add regression tests for provider behavior and follow up on review feedback promptly

## Alternatives Considered

### Skill

A skill is not the right fit here because it cannot cleanly participate in the memory-provider lifecycle, setup UX, or provider-managed auth/config.

### Private fork

A fork would work short-term, but it creates long-term divergence and makes official support less likely.

### Core MongoDB coupling

Rejected. The goal is an official provider plugin, not a hard dependency inside Hermes core.

## Feature Type

Other

## Scope

Medium (additive provider module + tests, no core refactor planned)

items.title: [Bug]: Feishu gateway intermittently drops inbound messages, delays reconnects, and may hang on shutdown
items.body:
### Bug Description

## Summary

The Feishu gateway has several websocket lifecycle issues that make message handling unreliable and process shutdown unsafe.

In practice, users can see intermittent message loss after reconnects, reconnect behavior that does not follow configured tuning, and gateway processes that do not exit cleanly after disconnect or stop.

## Problem

### 1. Inbound messages are intermittently dropped

Users can send Feishu messages successfully, but some inbound events are dropped without a response.

A common warning in logs is:

```text
WARNING gateway.platforms.feishu: [Feishu] Dropping inbound message before adapter loop is ready
```

This is especially confusing because it can continue appearing well after startup, including after the gateway has already connected and processed earlier messages successfully.

### 2. Reconnect timing is inconsistent and user tuning does not reliably take effect

After a websocket disconnect, reconnect behavior can appear unexpectedly slow or inconsistent.

Even when users provide custom Feishu websocket reconnect or ping settings, the runtime behavior may still look like the SDK defaults are being used.

This makes operational tuning difficult during unstable network conditions.

### 3. Gateway shutdown may hang

After stopping the gateway, the process may stay alive instead of exiting cleanly.

This can happen after Ctrl+C or other normal shutdown flows, suggesting that websocket-related background work is not being torn down fully.

## Impact

This affects Feishu gateway reliability in production:

- user messages may be silently dropped
- reconnect behavior is harder to control during incidents
- shutdown/restart workflows become less reliable
- operators may see misleading loop-readiness warnings long after startup

### Steps to Reproduce
